component.name: PQC Today Hub
component.description: PQC algorithm and product registry for post-quantum migration planning

components.name: BTQ Bitcoin Quantum
components.description: First quantum-safe fork of Bitcoin. Testnet v0.3.0 (Mar 2026) is the first working implementation of BIP-360 Pay-to-Merkle-Root (P2MR) outputs: SegWit v2 outputs with bc1z (bech32m) addresses, Merkle-root commitment verification, control-block validation, and all five Dilithium (ML-DSA) post-quantum signature opcodes enabled in P2MR tapscript context. Replaces ECDSA/Taproot internal-key exposure with NIST-standardized ML-DSA signatures. Testnet V3 surpassed 200,000 blocks and 50+ miners as of Mar 2026.

components.name: Hitachi DoMobile
components.description: DoMobile Ver.5 (Jan 2026) integrates 01 Quantum IronCAP PQC using FIPS 203 (ML-KEM). First in Japan.

components.name: Project Eleven Solana PQC
components.description: First post-quantum testnet for Solana blockchain developed in collaboration with Solana Foundation. Replaces EdDSA signatures with NIST-standardized ML-DSA demonstrating quantum-resistant transactions are practical on high-throughput blockchain architectures (65000+ TPS). Open-sourced testnet with readiness assessments and migration test environments. $20M Series A funding announced January 2026.

components.name: SEALSQ Quantum Shield QS7001
components.description: Post-quantum semiconductor-based trust anchors. QS7001 secure element supports ML-KEM-1024 and ML-DSA-87 (plus RSA, ECC, AES, SHA-1/2/3). QS7001 V1 reached production-sample availability in Mar 2026; V2 (full PQC algorithm API) targets engineering samples Jul 2026 and production samples Oct 2026. Common Criteria evaluation in progress via accredited labs (e.g. SERMA Technologies); V1 Hardware Evaluation Test Report expected end of Mar 2026, V2 ETR targeted Sep 2026. QVault-TPM line also tracks toward FIPS 140-3. Protects against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks.

components.name: Forward Edge-AI Isidore Quantum
components.description: Hardware-based plug-and-play post-quantum encryption platform. NSA CNSA 2.0 compliant protocol-agnostic solution working with legacy and modern networks. Features one-way data diode with NIST-approved PQC algorithms including ML-KEM. Tested by U.S. military branches with SpaceX deployment. Secures data in transit without software rewrites or PKI dependencies.

components.name: QuSecure QuProtect R3
components.description: First end-to-end cryptographic security platform for quantum era. Provides cryptographic discovery (Recon) crypto-agility engine (Resilience) and real-time compliance reporting. Enables dynamic cipher key and algorithm updates without code changes or downtime. Works across cloud on-premise and edge environments. Includes QuEverywhere for mobile PQC.

components.name: SandboxAQ AQtive Guard
components.description: Platform for automated discovery and inventory of cryptographic assets. Facilitates transition to post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM/FIPS 203, ML-DSA/FIPS 204, SLH-DSA/FIPS 205) and enhances cyber readiness. Provides continuous visibility into cryptographic dependencies. Deployed in U.S. Department of War (formerly DoD) CIO systems.

components.name: 01 Quantum IronCAP
components.description: Quantum-safe cryptographic engine using Modern McEliece, a patented optimization of Classic McEliece with Goppa code-based encryption, plus NIST-approved PQC algorithms and hash-based digital signatures. Not standard Classic McEliece. Powers Hitachi DoMobile Ver.5 remote access system in Japan. Developing Quantum AI Wrapper (QAW) for securing AI data with Full Homomorphic Encryption and Quantum Crypto Wrapper (QCW) for blockchain quantum-safety.

components.name: Bouncy Castle C# .NET
components.description: Implements ML-KEM (key exchange), ML-DSA and SLH-DSA (signature/authentication), and HQC for the .NET platform, including hybrid post-quantum TLS 1.3 cipher suites as of release 2.7.0.

components.name: Bouncy Castle Java LTS

Composite/hybrid classical-PQC signature support (available in mainline Java since 1.83) is not confirmed for the LTS branch — LTS is deliberately conservative, backporting a narrower feature set from mainline.

ML-KEM (Kyber) hybrid-encryption/KEM support is still under development, not yet in a stable release — the Hybrid Encryption API still offers only classical primitives.

components.name: Botan

components.name: SafeLogic CryptoComply
components.description: FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules. Supports hybrid mode (classical + PQC) and includes CryptoComply PQ TLS for quantum-safe data in transit. Drop-in OpenSSL compatibility. CryptoComply Go v4.0 adds all NIST PQC algorithms (ML-KEM FIPS 203 ML-DSA FIPS 204 SLH-DSA FIPS 205). PQC capabilities rolled out across Core v3.5 (OpenSSL-based) Mobile v3.5 Java v4 and Go v4.

components.name: SAP Cryptographic Library
components.description: Version 8.6 enables quantum-safe TLS 1.3 handshake using hybrid ECDHE-MLKEM key agreement based on X25519MLKEM768. ML-KEM is a standardized FIPS-203 algorithm for key encapsulation, preventing session key decryption by quantum computers.

components.name: PQShield PQSDK

components.name: Go stdlib crypto/mlkem
components.description: Native ML-KEM-768 and ML-KEM-1024 since Go 1.24 (Feb 2025). Hybrid post-quantum TLS enabled by default since Go 1.24 combining classical elliptic-curve cryptography with ML-KEM. Go 1.26 adds crypto/hpke and crypto/mlkem/mlkemtest packages with derandomized encapsulation for known-answer tests. FIPS 203 compliant.

components.name: RustCrypto ml-kem
components.description: Implements ML-KEM (formerly Kyber), a post-quantum secure key encapsulation mechanism standardized by NIST in FIPS 203. Supports three security levels: MlKem512, MlKem768, MlKem1024. Pure Rust implementation, version 0.3.2. Never independently audited.

components.name: RustCrypto ml-dsa
components.description: Implements ML-DSA (formerly CRYSTALS-Dilithium) per FIPS 204 final. Supports parameter sets MlDsa44 (Category 2), MlDsa65 (Category 3), and MlDsa87 (Category 5). Implementation is pure Rust, supports `no_std`, and includes key generation, signing, and verification. Warning: Never independently audited; use at own risk.

components.name: RustCrypto slh-dsa
components.description: Implements Stateless Hash-based Digital Signature Algorithm (SLH-DSA) based on SPHINCS+, finalized in NIST FIPS-205. Supports 12 parameter sets (SHA2 and SHAKE variants at L1, L3, L5 security). Signatures range from 7KB to 50KB. Implementation is not independently audited; requires Rust 1.75+.

components.name: pqm4

Integrates clean implementations from PQClean.

components.name: testssl.sh
components.description: testssl.sh is a testing/scanning tool, not a PQC implementation: it detects and reports which post-quantum algorithms a scanned TLS server supports. Its v3.2 CHANGELOG explicitly names checking six PQC/hybrid KEM groups (e.g. ML-KEM-based groups) and ML-DSA post-quantum signatures during a scan.

components.name: Cryptosense Analyzer
components.description: Provides continuous cryptographic inventory, risk assessment, and PQC migration planning. Cryptosense SA (now part of SandboxAQ) is a NIST NCCoE technology collaborator on the 'Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography' practice-guide project (crypto-discovery tooling) — it did not contribute to NIST's PQC algorithm standardization (FIPS 203/204/205).

components.name: ISARA Radiate
components.description: Production-ready SDK offering modular libraries for integrating PQC algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA). Supports hybrid certificates for migration. Achieves NIST PQC Security Level 5 on resource-limited devices. Includes MISRA-C compliant code and tools for validation of performance and interoperability between legacy and upgraded systems.

components.name: wolfBoot
components.description: wolfBoot 2.5.0 includes LMS/HSS (NIST SP 800-208, CNSA 2.0), XMSS/XMSS-MT, and ML-DSA up to level 5. Hybrid authentication (PQC + classic) supported.

components.name: Windows Server 2025
components.description: Windows Server 2025 includes ML-KEM and ML-DSA via CNG for TLS, code signing, VPN.

components.name: Android 16
components.description: Chrome/WebView inherited X25519+ML-KEM-768 hybrid TLS from BoringSSL (Chrome 131+, Nov 2024), providing browser-layer PQC. Native platform-level PQC (ML-DSA in AVB/Keystore, ML-KEM in Conscrypt) announced March 2026 for Android 17, not Android 16. Upgraded TLS 1.3 and Adiantum for data at rest protection.

components.name: iOS 26 / macOS 26
components.description: System-wide PQC support extending PQ3 iMessage. Apple's Platform Security Guide documents quantum-secure TLS enabled by default in URLSession/Network framework APIs (iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS/watchOS 26), quantum-secure VPN (native client + IKEv2 APIs), quantum-secure SSH key exchange (macOS 26), and quantum-secure iPhone-to-Apple-Watch pairing using ML-KEM. CryptoKit exposes ML-KEM 768/1024 and ML-DSA-65/87. Systems support quantum encryption only when connecting to a supporting server.

components.name: Juniper Junos OS
components.description: Junos OS 25.4R1 adds PQC signatures for software images (ML-DSA-87 + SHA-512, CNSA 2.0) on ACX/EX/MX/QFX/SRX. Separately, 'Quantum-Resistant Key Exchange in SSH' uses hybrid NTRU Prime 761 + X25519 (sntrup761x25519-sha512) — distinct from Junos's 'Quantum Buffer' feature, which only hardens classical Diffie-Hellman parameters and is not itself PQC. Quantum-safe IPsec VPN uses RFC 8784 post-quantum Pre-shared Key mixing in IKEv2 (plus optional QKD-sourced keys) — not an ML-KEM-based hybrid key exchange.

components.name: Palo Alto PAN-OS
components.description: Supports Post-Quantum Cryptography via PAN-OS 12.1 Orion. Features include a Quantum Readiness Dashboard for visibility, industry-first cipher translation to upgrade applications, and Quantum-Optimized Hardware (5th-gen NGFW models). Implements RFC 8784 (PPKs), RFC 9242, and RFC 9370 (Hybrid Keys) for IKEv2 VPNs. Supports integration with Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) per ETSI-014.

components.name: Fortinet FortiOS
components.description: FortiOS 7.6.1+ PQC IPsec via RFC 9370. KEMs: ML-KEM, BIKE, HQC, FRODO. Up to 7 rounds of key exchanges.

components.name: Check Point Quantum
components.description: R82 (Jumbo Hotfix Take 41+) adds Quantum Safe Key Exchange to IKEv2 VPN via RFC 9242/9370, using ML-KEM (FIPS 203; default pairs DH group 15 with Kyber768). ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, LMS, and XMSS are NOT implemented — they appear only in the vendor blog's background reference table (sourced from an NSA CNSA 2.0 explainer), not as Check Point features.

NOTE: GitHub repository was ARCHIVED by SandboxAQ on 2025-07-11 and is now read-only/unmaintained; final release v0.3.0 (2024-02-23, experimental TurboTLS + revamped Go bindings). components.name: Cloudflare CIRCL

Status is experimental; not recommended for production without caution.

components.name: Mullvad VPN App
components.description: Quantum-resistant WireGuard tunnels enabled by default on desktop (Windows/macOS/Linux), also available on iOS. ML-KEM (FIPS 203) replaced draft Kyber round 3 in app version 2024.9-beta1. HQC replaced Classic McEliece in app version 2025.7-beta1 (2025-06-04) for lower CPU cost and smaller public keys.

components.name: ExpressVPN Lightway
components.description: Lightway integrates ML-KEM (Module Lattice–Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism), the finalized NIST standard based on CRYSTALS-Kyber. It previously used Kyber and now uses a hybrid cryptography approach combining classical and post-quantum algorithms for seamless performance and future-proof security.

components.name: Tuta Mail
components.description: TutaCrypt protocol upgraded from Kyber to ML-KEM compatibility following NIST standardization. Hybrid encryption combining ML-KEM with X25519 ECDH. Enabled by default for all new accounts. Over 50% of existing users migrated to TutaCrypt protocol. Side-channel vulnerability mitigations applied to encryption libraries.

components.name: Keyfactor AgileSec Analytics
components.description: Enterprise cryptographic discovery and analytics platform (formerly InfoSec Global AgileSec). Automated scanning of network traffic and application code to inventory all cryptographic assets. Risk-based prioritization for PQC migration. SDK enables crypto-agile application development. Acquired by Keyfactor to integrate with EJBCA PKI and certificate lifecycle management.

components.name: Futurex CryptoHub
components.description: First HSM to receive PCI HSM validation with PQC support (June 2025). Supports ML-DSA and ML-KEM (FIPS 203/204 compliant), with SLH-DSA support described by Futurex as 'on the horizon' (not yet shipped) as of the June 2025 announcement, for financial and enterprise security.

components.name: Arqit Encryption Intelligence
components.description: Automated cryptographic discovery platform for post-quantum migration and compliance. Selected by UK NCSC for Post-Quantum Cryptography Pilot under Assured Cyber Security Consultancy Scheme. Available as SaaS or via certified systems integrator partners.

components.name: Samsung S3SSE2A eSE

Microsoft's PQC roadmap lists BitLocker PQC integration only as an unscheduled 'future direction' (progress expected 'this year', more in 2027) — no algorithm, hardware, or date is actually committed.

components.name: CockroachDB Encryption
components.description: CockroachDB uses Go crypto/tls which in Go 1.24+ enables X25519MLKEM768 hybrid PQC by default.

components.name: Proton Mail
components.description: Post-quantum protection launched generally May 5, 2026, available on all Proton Mail plans including free (rolled out gradually). Adds support for OpenPGP v6 enabling post-quantum (PQC) encryption keys; protects new encrypted emails going forward with planned re-encryption of older mail. Classical RSA/ECC retained as a layer alongside PQC. Underlying KEM is ML-KEM-based (hybrid).

components.name: GnuPG
components.description: GnuPG's 2.5.x development series (2.5.20, released 2026-05-13) ships Kyber/ML-KEM (FIPS 203) as a post-quantum KEM for OpenPGP encryption, always used in a composite scheme with a classical ECC algorithm. No PQC signature algorithm (ML-DSA) yet — encryption-only so far. Current stable 2.4.x line has no PQC and is nearing end-of-life; PQC is expected to carry into the next stable 2.6 series.

components.name: DigiCert SigningHub

It mentions a blog post titled "No Time to Wait: PQC Pressure from the Dept. of War" but does not detail specific PQC algorithms, implementation status, or maturity levels for the product itself.

X25519MLKEM768/SecP256r1MLKEM768 are only available in HAProxy Technologies' own vendor builds (Enterprise or Community Performance Packages), not a generic self-compiled build.

components.name: AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB)
components.description: Managed load balancing service. AWS rolled out hybrid ML-KEM TLS support to ALB and NLB endpoints enabling enterprises to achieve quantum-safe data-in-transit without modifying application code.

components.name: Cloudflare Edge Network
components.description: Deploys X25519MLKEM768 post-quantum hybrid key agreement across Cloudflare's edge network (default in major browsers since late 2024); ML-DSA (evaluating ML-DSA-44) is not yet deployed, only under evaluation. Supported via Cloudflare's fork of Go, OpenSSL 3.5.0+, Node.js, BoringSSL, GnuTLS, rustls, and NGINX.

properties.name: pqctoday:algorithm_implementations
properties.value: SecP256r1MLKEM768 (Cloudflare PQ TLS); SecP384r1MLKEM1024 (Cloudflare PQ TLS); X25519MLKEM768 (Cloudflare PQ TLS)

components.name: Keyfactor Command
components.description: Command 25.3 (Oct 2025) issues, inventories, and enrolls hybrid and PQ certificates using NIST-approved ML-DSA and newly added SLH-DSA algorithms (hybrid classical + quantum-safe). 25.1 added hybrid RSA/ML-DSA enrollment; 25.2 added ML-DSA hybrid + PQC enrollment via CSR/PFX.

components.name: Venafi TLS Protect
components.description: Experimental PQC certificate issuance: ML-DSA and SLH-DSA (plus Falcon, scoped to TLS certificates only) are available for certificates created in TLS Protect, but PQC must first be enabled on the underlying Trust Protection Platform server. No ML-KEM or hybrid key-establishment support is documented.

components.name: AppViewX CERT+
components.description: Automated certificate lifecycle management platform. PQC certificate issuance planned via integration with DigiCert, Entrust, and Sectigo CAs supporting ML-DSA. Crypto-agility engine targets automated bulk migration from RSA/ECDSA to PQC certificates.

components.name: Keycloak
components.description: Not stated in the provided text.

components.name: Thales CipherTrust Data Security Platform
components.description: Unified data security platform combining CipherTrust Manager, transparent encryption (CTE), tokenization, and key management. Integrates with Thales Luna HSMs (firmware 7.9+) supporting ML-KEM and ML-DSA. Provides quantum-safe encryption for structured and unstructured data at rest.

components.name: Virtru Data Protection
components.description: Not stated in the document. The text mentions "open standards" and "Trusted Data Format" but does not specify Post-Quantum Cryptography algorithms, readiness, or migration plans.

components.name: Intel TDX (Trust Domain Extensions)
components.description: Intel TDX provides hardware-isolated Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) at the VM level using architectural extensions on 4th/5th Gen Xeon processors. TDX Trust Domains protect data-in-use from hypervisor and host OS. Current remote attestation uses ECDSA P-256 via Intel PCS, with no Intel-published PQC migration timeline for attestation signing. Arqit, a partner, delivers quantum-safe symmetric key agreement for network traffic between workloads running inside TDX Trust Domains -- this is a workload/network-layer capability enabled on top of TDX, not a TDX-native attestation or memory-sealing feature.

components.name: Google Cloud KMS
components.description: ML-DSA parameter sets: ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, ML-DSA-87 (each also with an External-mu variant), plus SLH-DSA-SHA2-128S (Pure and Pre-hash). KEM support: ML-KEM-768, ML-KEM-1024, and X-Wing (hybrid ML-KEM-768 + X25519, recommended default).

properties.name: pqctoday:fips_validated
properties.value: Yes (FIPS 140-2 L1 software / L3 Cloud HSM)

components.name: AWS KMS
components.description: ML-DSA digital signatures (FIPS 204) GA since June 2025 with ML-DSA-44/65/87 key specs via CreateKey/Sign/Verify APIs in FIPS 140-3 L3 HSMs. ML-KEM hybrid TLS for API transit protection via AWS-LC. PQC key import (BYOK) not supported — ML-DSA keys must be generated in KMS. External Key Store (XKS) symmetric-only — no PQC HYOK. AWS Private CA supports ML-DSA certificate issuance for code signing workflows.

components.name: Thales Luna Cloud HSM (DPoD)
components.version: Per Thales's official Luna Cloud HSM Customer Release Notes (last updated 2026-06-19), current entries are 'Luna Cloud HSM Firmware Version 3.0' (rollout: NA/EU FIPS H2 2026, NA/EU non-FIPS H2 2025) and 'HSM Client 10.9.0' (released July 2025) — not 'Luna HSM Firmware v7.9.2 (Software v7.9.1, UC v10.9.2)'. Luna Cloud HSM uses its own version track, distinct from the on-premises Luna Network HSM's 7.9.x firmware numbering.
components.description: No evidence found that Luna Cloud HSM (the DPoD service) itself supports ML-KEM/ML-DSA/LMS-HSS as of 2026-06-19. PQC support (ML-KEM FIPS 203, ML-DSA FIPS 204, HSS per NIST SP 800-208) is confirmed by Thales's July-2026 solution brief only for on-premises/dedicated Luna 7-family hardware (Luna Network, PCIe, USB, Backup HSM) — not for the Luna Cloud HSM service.

properties.name: pqctoday:fips_validated
properties.value: Yes (FIPS 140-2 L3); FIPS 140-3 Level 3 compliance updates in v7.9.2 — next FIPS candidate with PQC (validation in progress)

components.name: AWS CloudHSM
components.description: Dedicated managed HSM service in AWS (FIPS 140-2 L3). ML-KEM-768 and ML-DSA-65 available through AWS Crypto Tools SDK integration. Native PKCS#11 PQC mechanisms not yet available in firmware. AWS KMS provides PQC TLS endpoints with ML-KEM hybrid. Managed service with multi-AZ redundancy.

components.name: Toshiba QKD System
components.description: Toshiba's Key Distribution System now integrates post-quantum cryptography (PQC) key exchange in a hybrid QKD+PQC architecture to bridge geographically separated/intercontinental QKD networks without additional hardware (announced Mar 2, 2026). Demonstrated at OFC 2026 (May 2026) with Quantum Bridge Technologies connecting metro QKD networks in Cambridge UK and Toronto, Canada. Specific NIST PQC algorithm names not disclosed. Underlying QKD includes multiplexed QKD (33.4 Tbps over 80 km, Mar 2025) and coherent quantum communication (Apr 2025).

components.name: Thales High Speed Encryptor (HSE)
components.description: Crypto-agile high-speed network encryptors. Built on field-upgradable FPGAs, Thales High Speed Encryptors (HSEs) support ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205), alongside unspecified sovereign algorithms, via field-upgradable firmware for the PQC transition. HSEs integrate with Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) devices for key delivery over optical links and can incorporate Quantum Random Number Generation (QRNG) for high-entropy key derivation. Transport Independent Mode (TIM) enables symmetric key derivation without public key exchange.

components.name: Senetas CN7000 Series
components.description: COTS hardware-based, crypto-agile network encryptors (CN7105, CN7107, CN7108) supporting ML-KEM and ML-DSA for quantum-resistant hybrid encryption. First-to-market with Quantum Resistant Encryption (QRE) supporting hybrid classical+PQC key exchange. Field-updateable without hardware replacement. Certified under Malaysia PKTN scheme (Confidential classification, September 2025). Supports both QKD and PQC hybrid deployments for critical infrastructure.

properties.name: pqctoday:fips_validated
properties.value: Yes (PKTN Confidential / Common Criteria) (classical algorithms only; PQC not in FIPS scope)

components.name: Adva Network Security FSP 3000 S-Flex
components.description: World-first BSI-approved 400G quantum-safe Layer 1 network encryptor (September 2025). Uses AES-256 with hybrid crypto-agile key exchange combining PQC and classical Diffie-Hellman. ConnectGuard technology provides ultra-low-latency encryption. Protects against Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later attacks. Confirmed via the official FSP 3000 S-Flex data sheet (updated July 14, 2026): 'Hybrid key exchange: DH4096 + ML-KEM-1024' — the PQC algorithm is ML-KEM-1024 (FIPS 203), not Classic McEliece; the prior 'could not be confirmed' hedge is resolved.

components.name: Ciena WaveLogic 6 Extreme
components.description: Industry-leading 1.6 Tbps quantum-safe optical transport encryption. WaveLogic 6 Extreme integrates NIST PQC algorithms with AES-256-GCM in hybrid mode and supports QKD vendor interoperability for defense-in-depth quantum security. Protects long-distance DWDM optical networks at Layer 1. Existing WaveLogic 5e 800G deployments upgradeable via software.

components.name: EJBCA
components.description: Supports NIST-approved post-quantum algorithms ML-DSA and ML-KEM (FIPS 204/203) since EJBCA 9.1 (November 2024), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) since EJBCA 9.3 (June 2025) — both stable, generally-available features, not behind an experimental flag. EJBCA 9.3 also added HSM-backed integration for ML-DSA via REST API-based HSMs. FN-DSA (derived from FALCON) is not yet supported: Keyfactor's official docs state it 'will follow' once NIST finalizes that standard. Enables certificate/key inventory and creation of post-quantum CAs and code-signing certificates using these algorithms. (Earlier EJBCA 8.0, 2023, supported the pre-standardization candidate names Dilithium, Falcon, and SPHINCS+ for testing/evaluation only; superseded by the NIST-final names in 9.1/9.3.)

components.name: DigiCert Trust Lifecycle Manager
components.description: Supports issuing and managing (revoke, suspend/resume, escrow/recover) private PQC certificates using ML-DSA or SLH-DSA algorithms. Includes network scans for discovery. Does not currently support Falcon or Composite PQC certificates as they are experimental; testing available via DigiCert LABS.

components.name: IBM Guardium Quantum Safe
components.description: Enterprise platform for cryptographic discovery and quantum-safe posture management, delivered as an independent, separately-installable module of IBM Guardium Data Security Center (marketed since late 2025 under the product name IBM Guardium Cryptography Manager). Builds its cryptographic inventory from network scanning, application provisioning, and CMDB data, and ingests a Cryptography Bill of Materials (CBOM) produced by the companion IBM Quantum Safe Explorer tool, which performs the actual source-code/binary scanning. Provides risk-based prioritization of quantum-vulnerable algorithms, policy enforcement/alerting, and remediation-ticket integration with ServiceNow and Jira. Part of IBM's Quantum Safe enterprise software portfolio alongside IBM Quantum Safe Explorer and IBM Quantum Safe Remediator — not the Qiskit SDK, which is IBM's unrelated quantum-computing programming toolkit.

components.name: Google Chrome
components.description: Chrome 131+ defaults to X25519MLKEM768 (hybrid X25519 + ML-KEM-768) for TLS 1.3/QUIC key exchange on all desktop platforms, providing quantum-resistant confidentiality only. Chrome does not use post-quantum signatures for TLS certificate/server authentication. Separately, Chrome 151+ (July 2026) exposes ML-DSA-44/65/87 as JavaScript-callable primitives in the Web Cryptography API, but only behind an opt-in Origin Trial — not enabled by default. SLH-DSA is not present in any current or proposed Chrome feature.

components.name: Microsoft Edge
components.description: Post-quantum key agreement (hybrid X25519+ML-KEM, via X25519MLKEM768) enabled by default in Edge 131+, replacing the earlier draft Kyber implementation used in Edge 124-130. Since Edge 147, this can no longer be disabled by administrators (the PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled policy was removed).

components.name: Mozilla Firefox
components.description: Firefox 132 enabled the post-quantum hybrid key exchange X25519MLKEM768 (mlkem768x25519) BY DEFAULT for TLS 1.3 HTTPS connections (Bugzilla bug 1919097: pref security.tls.enable_kyber flipped to true by default on desktop). Firefox 135 extended default support to HTTP/3 (QUIC).

components.name: Apple Safari
components.description: iMessage PQ3 in iOS 17.4+. Safari inherits quantum-secure TLS via the system CFNetwork/Network.framework/URLSession stack (Safari has no separate TLS implementation of its own): TLS 1.3 with X25519MLKEM768 hybrid key exchange is enabled by default on iOS 26/iPadOS 26/macOS Tahoe 26+. Per Apple's Platform Security Guide: 'Internet apps such as Safari... automatically use this protocol... TLS 1.3 with quantum-secure encryption (with the X25519MLKEM768 key exchange algorithm) is enabled by default for URLSession framework and the Network APIs.' CryptoKit PQC support for app developers.

properties.name: pqctoday:fips_validated
properties.value: No (CoreCrypto FIPS exists for classical algorithms; PQC not in FIPS scope)

components.name: Crypto4A QxHSM
components.description: First HSM submitted for FIPS 140-3 Level 3 certification with all NIST PQC algorithms. Powered by the QASM cryptographic core natively supporting ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), SLH-DSA (FIPS 205), and LMS stateful hash-based signatures. QxHSM v4.4 (Dec 2024) added ML-DSA and full NIST PQC OID support. QxOS 5 firmware (June 2025) delivers next-generation quantum-safe HSM platform. FIPS 140-3 Level 3 certification submitted March 2025, currently in NIST MIP list. Available in desktop (QxBMC-1) and 1U three-blade (QxBMC-3) chassis; the 4U twelve-blade (QxBMC-12) chassis is listed by the vendor as 'Coming Soon' and not yet shipping. Engineered, manufactured, and assembled in Canada.

components.name: Securosys CloudHSM
components.description: HSM-as-a-Service built on Swiss Primus HSM hardware delivering full post-quantum cryptography support. Supports ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), SLH-DSA (FIPS 205), plus stateful hash-based signatures HSS-LMS and XMSS. Includes CloudHSM SBX (Sandbox) for testing PQC migration strategies with dual HSM synchronization before production rollout. REST API access via Transaction Security Broker (TSB) middleware — language-agnostic integration without client libraries. Available in multiple service tiers: ECO (Economy, shared multi-tenant) for smaller workloads, SBX (Sandbox) for pre-production testing, and Platinum (PLT, dedicated HSM) for production — Securosys CloudHSM has no tier named 'Enterprise'. Swiss infrastructure; same FIPS 140-2 Level 3 and CC EAL4+ validated hardware as Primus HSM.

components.name: Imperva WAF
components.description: Imperva Cloud WAF supports quantum-resistant ciphers in hybrid mode for visitor-to-service TLS connectivity. Made available as opt-in in Q3 2025 and enabled by default in Q4 2025. Requires only a configuration change with no origin-server upgrade. Specific hybrid named groups (e.g. X25519MLKEM768) not explicitly enumerated in the public material reviewed.

components.name: Venafi CodeSign Protect
components.description: Enterprise code signing platform, now branded CyberArk Code Sign Manager - Self-Hosted (formerly Venafi CodeSign Protect), running on CyberArk Trust Protection Foundation (formerly Trust Protection Platform). PQC signing key algorithm support, present since v24.1 and current through v26.1 (July 2026), covers ML-DSA (CRYSTALS-Dilithium; NIST FIPS 204, parameter sets ML-DSA-44/65/87) and SLH-DSA (SPHINCS+; NIST FIPS 205, SHA2/SHAKE and HASH-SLH-DSA parameter sets) for Certificate and Key Pair environments. Falcon is documented separately and applies only to TLS server certificates, not code signing. Supported through CodeSign Protect/Code Sign Manager clients, the libhsm API, and PKCS#11. As of the 24.3 documentation, PQC environments were required to use 'Software' as the key storage location (no HSM support for PQC keys); the page carrying that specific restriction was retired in the 25.1/26.1 documentation reorganization and no current source confirms or contradicts it — HSM support for PQC keys should be reconfirmed directly, not assumed changed.

components.name: RPM Signing (rpm-sign)
components.description: RPM 6.0 (backported into RHEL 10.1, GA'd November 12, 2025) supports hybrid ML-DSA-87+Ed448 package signing via Sequoia-PGP with OpenPGP v6. Red Hat's own authoritative source (last updated Feb 27, 2026) still describes this as a 'technology preview... not intended for production use.' Red Hat has begun signing select RHEL 10.1 packages (e.g. ipmitool-1.8.19-10.el10_1, RHBA-2025:23156) with the hybrid key alongside the existing RSA signature — sources found do not support 'all Red Hat products' being PQC-signed. Red Hat states (in separate blog posts, not the cited authoritative_source) that RHEL is 'the first and currently only major Linux distribution' to reach this milestone. RPM v6 packages support multiple signatures per package.

components.name: Garantir GaraTrust
components.description: Garantir's live Enterprise Code Signing product page states, in direct present-tense answer to its own FAQ ('Is GaraTrust ready for post-quantum cryptography (PQC)?'): 'Yes. The GaraTrust signing infrastructure provides quantum-agile hybrid support, combining classical RSA/ECC and post-quantum primitives. We offer both stateless (ML-DSA) for general purpose software distribution and stateful (LMS) signatures optimized for high-assurance firmware and hardware roots-of-trust.' This confirms current, production support for ML-DSA and LMS within the code-signing product specifically. XMSS is not mentioned anywhere on this page, the main GaraTrust platform page, or the official datasheet PDF. The main platform page instead frames post-quantum algorithms (ML-DSA, LMS, and also SLH-DSA) as the end-state of a crypto-agility roadmap for the rest of the platform, i.e. still forward-looking outside code signing.

components.name: Java jarsigner (JDK)
components.description: JDK 24 (March 2025) introduced ML-KEM and ML-DSA as JCA providers via JEP 496/497. JDK 26 (released March 17, 2026) adds signed JAR support for ML-DSA, so jarsigner can now sign JARs with ML-DSA (e.g. ML-DSA-65) per JDK-8349732. JDK 26 also adds an HPKE (Hybrid Public Key Encryption) API (initially traditional/non-PQC algorithms, with PQC planned once RFCs finalize). The X25519MLKEM768 post-quantum hybrid TLS named group is NOT part of JDK 26 — it ships via JEP 527 (Post-Quantum Hybrid Key Exchange for TLS 1.3), whose JBS ticket shows Fix Version 27, resolved 2026-04-22 (after JDK 26 GA). JEP 527 is integrated into JDK 27 early-access builds and targets JDK 27 GA (scheduled September 15, 2026, currently in Release Candidate phase).

components.name: Mbed TLS
components.description: ARM TrustedFirmware TLS library widely used in embedded IoT devices. LMS hash-based signatures available for verification. TF-PSA-Crypto 1.1 LTS and Mbed TLS 4.1 (paired LTS releases, supported until at least March 2029) shipped on schedule at the end of Q1 2026 (2026-03-31, per GitHub Releases API). ML-DSA 'Initial support' was targeted for Q2 2026 on the official roadmap but has NOT shipped as of the latest release (Mbed TLS 4.2.0 / TF-PSA-Crypto 1.2.0, 2026-07-07) — no ML-DSA identifiers appear in any release changelog since 4.1.0, nor in the current unreleased development branch's public PSA Crypto API headers, indicating the target has slipped past its quarter. ML-KEM remains listed as Future on the roadmap (not scheduled). Critical gap for IoT/embedded PQC migration as millions of devices depend on Mbed TLS.

components.name: NSS (Mozilla)
components.description: Supports NIST-approved PQC algorithms ML-KEM (for key exchange) and ML-DSA (for digital signatures), with support added and expanded incrementally across NSS releases from 3.116 (September 2025) through at least 3.126 (July 2026); Mozilla's own NSS 3.112 (May 2025) release notes contain no ML-KEM/ML-DSA content. FIPS 140-3 compliant code is open-sourced. The module has achieved CAVP certification and entered the Modules in Process (MIP) list, with full FIPS validation anticipated Q2 2027.

components.name: .NET System.Security.Cryptography
components.description: .NET 10 (Nov 2025 GA) provides native PQC APIs: MLKem class (FIPS 203), MLDsa class (FIPS 204), SlhDsa class (FIPS 205), and CompositeMLDsa class for composite signatures. Per Microsoft's own .NET 10 documentation, only the SlhDsa and CompositeMLDsa classes are marked [Experimental] under diagnostic SYSLIB5006 (pending full OS-level platform support for SLH-DSA and Composite ML-DSA); the MLKem and MLDsa classes themselves are not marked [Experimental], though a handful of their methods still carry the SYSLIB5006 diagnostic. Microsoft's documentation does not describe any of these APIs as 'production-ready'; Experimental-flagged types are explicitly described as subject to potential breaking structural changes until platform support is complete. Uses Windows CNG on Windows and OpenSSL 3.5+ on Linux. First-party Microsoft implementation with all three NIST PQC standards available to every .NET 10 application.

components.name: Thales Luna T-Series HSM
components.description: Government and defense HSM with v7.15.0 delivering ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and ML-DSA (FIPS 204) implementations. Also supports LMS/HSS (SP 800-208). Industry-first FIPS 140-compliant HSM with embedded Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) chip for quantum-enhanced key generation. Made in USA. CNSA 2.0 aligned. Note: FN-DSA (Falcon/FIPS 206) is NOT confirmed in v7.15.0 — FIPS 206 draft not yet finalized by NIST.

components.name: Thales MISTRAL Encryptor
components.description: MISTRAL PQC encryptor unveiled Nov 2025 (European Cyber Week); still in operational testing at announcement, with commercial availability targeted for June 2026 — specific PQC algorithm not publicly disclosed by Thales. ANSSI-aligned, CC EAL4+, 4x10 Gbps.

properties.name: pqctoday:fips_validated
properties.value: No (CC EAL4+ targeted) (classical algorithms only; PQC not in FIPS scope)

components.name: Thales CipherTrust Cloud Key Manager
components.description: Cloud key management for BYOK/HYOK across AWS Azure GCP and Google Workspace. Quantum-resilient TLS ciphers for Chrome/CCKM connections (GA v2.22.0, Dec 2025) for Google Workspace CSE connections between Chrome and CM/CCKM. ML-KEM-enabled channels for Google Workspace CSE BYOK key rotation. BYOK key rotation for AWS KMS supported since v2.19; automated multi-account and on-demand rotation added in v2.21.0. SAP BYOK integration available (GA since v2.19, Feb 2025). Current CipherTrust Manager/CCKM platform version: 2.23.0 LTS (July 2026).

components.name: HashiCorp Vault Transit
components.description: Vault Enterprise 1.19+ transit secrets engine supports experimental PQC signing: ML-DSA-44/65/87 (FIPS 204) and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) with 12 parameter sets (SHA2/SHAKE 128/192/256 s/f variants). Hybrid signatures combining ML-DSA with ecdsa-p256 ecdsa-p384 ecdsa-p521 or ed25519. Marked experimental and not recommended for production workloads. HashiCorp plans staged PQC delivery across additional Vault capabilities.

components.name: Windows 11
components.version: 25H2 (Build 26200, latest cumulative 26200.9168) is the current general-availability release as of Aug 2026. 24H2 (Build 26100.9168) remains concurrently serviced.
components.description: PQC is Generally Available (GA) in Windows 11 (24H2, 25H2) and Server 2025 via CNG updates (GA since Nov 2025). Supports ML-KEM (Key Encapsulation, FIPS 203) and ML-DSA (Digital Signatures, FIPS 204). Composite ML-KEM and composite ML-DSA (classical+PQ) shipped via KB5095093 (Jun 2026). Certificate store supports installing/importing/exporting ML-DSA certificates and validating PQ certificate chains. TLS hybrid key exchange in Schannel is now Generally Available (GA) as of July 14, 2026 (KB5089573 for 24H2/25H2, KB5095091 for 26H1) with three configurable groups — x25519_mlkem768, secp256r1_mlkem768, secp384r1_mlkem1024 — disabled by default and enabled via Group Policy, MDM, or TLS PowerShell cmdlets. It is no longer 'planned' or Linux-only.

properties.name: pqctoday:fips_validated
properties.value: Partial (CNG FIPS 140-3; PQC module under review)

components.name: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9
components.description: RHEL 9.7 introduced the PQ crypto-policies subpolicy enabling hybrid ML-KEM and pure ML-DSA (ML-DSA-44/65/87) for NSS, OpenSSL, and Sequoia PGP. RHEL 9.8 (current, released 2026-05-20) extended PQ subpolicy support to GnuTLS (hybrid ML-KEM + pure ML-DSA for TLS) and added ML-KEM key exchange (mlkem768x25519-sha256) for OpenSSH, which 9.7 lacked.

properties.name: pqctoday:fips_validated
properties.value: Partial (OpenSSL FIPS 140-3; PQC not in FIPS module)

components.name: Fedora Linux
components.description: Fedora 44 (current stable, released 2026-04-28) and Fedora 43 ship OpenSSL 3.5 (3.5.7) with native ML-KEM and ML-DSA; oqsprovider is no longer needed and the DEFAULT crypto-policy supports PQ algorithms out of the box. Fedora 42 used the TEST-PQ crypto-policy with oqsprovider bridging OpenSSL 3.2 to liboqs. Hybrid signature schemes are not yet available in OpenSSL 3.5 (Fedora Rawhide/Fedora 45 has since moved to OpenSSL 4.0.1).

components.name: Debian 13 (Trixie)
components.description: Debian 13 (Trixie), released 2025-08-09, ships OpenSSL 3.5.6 (package openssl 3.5.6-1~deb13u2; siblings openssl-provider-legacy 3.5.5, openssl-provider-fips 3.5.4), confirmed on packages.debian.org/tr

components.name: Ericsson Quantum-Safe 5G
components.description: Experimental simulation environment evaluating PQC integration in 5G Core registration/deregistration. Uses hybrid schemes combining conventional and PQC algorithms. Tested KEMs: BIKE, FrodoKEM. Tested Signatures: ML-DSA (Dilithium), SLH-DSA (SPHINCS+), Falcon (FN-DSA). Also evaluated secp256r1 and RSA for comparison.

components.name: Nokia Quantum-Safe Networks
components.description: Nokia defense-in-depth approach combining PQC and QKD for quantum-safe 5G networks. NetGuard suite includes Certificate Manager and Identity Access Manager for telecom security. Quantum-safe optical transport via the Nokia 1830 Security Management Server (SMS) with encryption engines on 1830 PSS/PSS-x and 1830 PSI platforms (AES-256 symmetric-key architecture) — not PSE-V, which is Nokia's coherent-optics DSP chipset family for capacity/reach and has no encryption function of its own. IPsec Security Gateway (IP network layer) already supports quantum-safe/PQC cryptography today, demonstrated live with Turkcell (Dec 2024). Satellite QKD trial with Colt and Honeywell (announced Jun 2025; LEO QKD demo targeted Q3 2026, still pending as of Aug 2026; production launch targeted Q3 2027). Active 3GPP SA3 (security working group) contributor — Nokia has chaired SA3 for the past four years and drove approval of a follow-up PQC study for 5G/6G.

components.name: Thales 5G Quantum-Safe SIM
components.description: Quantum-safe 5G SIM demonstrated with SK Telecom on commercial 5G standalone network. ML-KEM algorithm implemented natively in SIM operating system for quantum-resistant subscriber identity concealment (SUCI). Hybrid key exchange combining traditional asymmetric and PQC algorithms. Protects user SUPI from Harvest Now Decrypt Later attacks. [Note: release date predates FIPS 203/204/205 finalization (Aug 2024); may reference draft/pre-standard algorithms.]

components.name: G+D Quantum-Safe SIM Platform
components.description: G+D is developing prototypes in Digital Security, Financial Platforms, and Currency Technology segments. The company states it is positioned to deliver products enhanced with PQC capabilities as standards become finalized. No specific algorithms or production-ready status for the SIM platform itself are stated; only general involvement in standardization and prototype development is mentioned.

components.name: Samsung Knox Quantum-Safe
components.description: First mobile platform to ship PQC-based cloud data protection. Galaxy S25 series (One UI 7) integrates ML-KEM into Knox Matrix for quantum-safe Samsung Cloud backup restore and sync. One UI 8 expands with ML-KEM Secure Wi-Fi and Knox Enhanced Encrypted Protection (KEEP).

components.name: IDEMIA PQC Secure Element
components.description: First hardware accelerator designed for post-quantum cryptography using Keccak-based technology. Offloads ML-KEM (FIPS 203) ML-DSA (FIPS 204) and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) computations from main processor. Embedded in future IDEMIA quantum-safe chips for banking SIM automotive IoT and healthcare secure elements. Supports crypto-agility framework.

components.name: IDEMIA Digital Identity Platform
components.description: IDEMIA Secure Transactions positions itself as an early crypto-agility provider and offers ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, LMS and ML-KEM via its Sphere Cryptographic Library — but that is a separate Cybersecurity/embedded-devices product line, not part of the identity platform. For identity credentials specifically, IDEMIA's own 2026 white paper (IDEMIA Public Security) states PIV/FIDO protocols 'have not yet evolved to a quantum-safe version,' and describes crypto-agility for identity hardware tokens as still at the 'first step' sandbox proof-of-concept stage. The only concrete PQC demonstration found (MWC 2025, crypto-agile TLS on quantum-ready industrial equipment) was performed by IDEMIA Secure Transactions, not the identity/Public Security division. No evidence was found that IDEMIA participated in the Bundesdruckerei/BSI/Infineon German quantum-secure ID card proof-of-concept (announced Nov 2025) — that program's actual technology partner is Giesecke+Devrient (G+D), a competitor, per both Bundesdruckerei's own press release and independent coverage. No IDEMIA-published source ties PQC to an eIDAS 2.0/EUDI Wallet credential-issuance roadmap.

components.name: Procivis One
components.description: Modular open-source digital identity platform with ML-DSA support for verifiable credentials. Compliant with eIDAS 2.0 Swiss E-ID and ISO 18013-5 mDL standards. Supports W3C VCDM SD-JWT VC and OID4VC protocols. Delivered Lithuanian EU digital identity wallet sandbox.

components.name: Microsoft Entra Verified ID
components.description: PQC is not currently enabled for this specific product but is part of a broader Microsoft Quantum Safe Program (QSP). As of June 30, 2026, Microsoft accelerated the QSP roadmap: the goal is now to transition products and services to PQC by 2029, a four-year pull-forward from the previously stated 2033 full-transition target. Foundational components like SymCrypt already support ML-KEM and ML-DSA, which underpin future service updates including identity services such as Entra.

components.name: Wire
components.description: The document mentions "ciphersuite agility" in the context of MLS to allow future algorithm negotiation, but explicitly states current use of the Proteus Protocol (DoubleRatchet) and does not list any specific Post-Quantum Cryptography algorithms or implementations.

components.name: Element (Matrix Protocol)
components.description: Element (built on the Matrix protocol) has post-quantum encryption on its roadmap; a PQXDH-style handshake (X3DH extended with ML-KEM/Kyber) has been under development on the vodozemac crypto library, but per Matrix.org's own Dec 2025 status update this is not yet shipped -- Post-Quantum encryption remains listed among items still 'to progress'.

components.name: Oracle AI Database 26ai
components.description: Oracle AI Database 26ai supports quantum-resistant TLS 1.3 via ML-KEM key exchange (hybrid ECDHE + ML-KEM). ML-DSA certificate support for database authentication (requires JDK 24+). PQC crypto provided by Oracle OpenSSL FIPS Provider (ACVP A7758).

components.name: Microsoft Entra ID
components.description: PQC capabilities are previewed for Windows Insiders and Linux via SymCrypt updates supporting ML-KEM and ML-DSA. Microsoft Entra authentication is identified as a core infrastructure service for quantum safety transition. Full maturity expected by 2033, with early adoption starting in 2029 using hybrid or direct PQC approaches.

components.name: Thales MultiApp 5.2 Premium PQC
components.description: Europe's first ANSSI Common Criteria EAL6+ certified quantum-resistant smart card. Implements ML-DSA (FIPS 204) lattice-based digital signatures for quantum-safe identity protection. Designed for national ID cards health cards and driving licenses. Crypto-agile architecture supports classical and PQC algorithms simultaneously.

components.name: Infineon TEGRION SLC27 PQC
components.description: Infineon TEGRION SLC27 contactless/dual-interface security controller (Integrity Guard 32 architecture) with a Common Criteria EAL6+ certified cryptography library featuring the PQC algorithms ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and ML-DSA (FIPS 204). Supports in-field updates and crypto agility for long-life products such as ePassports, IoT devices and Secure Elements. Announced October 2025; available as sample and for high-volume orders.

components.name: hash-sigs
components.description: Reference C implementation of LMS and HSS stateful hash-based signatures per RFC 8554 (based on draft-mcgrew-hash-sigs, co-authored by David McGrew of Cisco). Supports all LMS/LM-OTS parameter sets defined in RFC 8554 (SHA-256, 256-bit output, tree heights 5/10/15/20/25, Winternitz W1/W2/W4/W8) — i.e., only the SHA-256(N32) family of parameter sets that NIST SP 800-208 approves; it does NOT implement the additional SHA-256/192, SHAKE256/256, or SHAKE256/192 parameter sets that SP 800-208 also approves. Full key generation, signing, and verification. Used as an external integration basis by wolfSSL/wolfCrypt (per wolfBoot's own manual: 'The external LMS/HSS support in wolfCrypt requires the hash-sigs library').

components.name: xmss-reference
components.description: Official C reference implementation of XMSS and XMSS^MT per RFC 8391, originally written by two of the RFC's five authors (Andreas Hülsing and Joost Rijneveld). Covers all RFC 8391 parameter sets with SHA-2 and SHAKE hash functions. Includes key generation, signing, verification, and state persistence. Repository has had no commits since 2021-03-16 and multiple open issues (some dating to 2019) remain unaddressed, indicating it is effectively unmaintained rather than actively maintained. Historically used as a canonical cross-validation reference for other XMSS implementations.

components.name: Azure Dedicated HSM (Thales Luna 7)
components.description: Azure Dedicated HSM is a single-tenant HSM service running Thales Luna Network HSM 7 model A790 appliances (stated in Microsoft's own Dedicated HSM overview). PQC arrives with Thales Luna firmware v7.9.2+, applied on customer request via Azure Support rather than automatically. Microsoft has announced the service is retiring: no new customer onboardings, full support for existing customers to 31 July 2028.

properties.name: pqctoday:fips_validated
properties.value: Yes (FIPS 140-2 Level 3) (classical algorithms only; PQC not in FIPS scope)

components.name: IBM Hyper Protect Crypto Services
components.description: IBM Hyper Protect Crypto Services uses IBM proprietary 4769 CEX hardware (FIPS 140-2 Level 4). IBM Quantum Safe initiative targets ML-KEM and ML-DSA support; not GA as of June 2026.

components.name: IBM Cloud HSM (Utimaco)
components.description: IBM Cloud HSM uses Utimaco SecurityServer hardware backend. FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated. IBM Quantum Safe roadmap includes HSM firmware updates for ML-KEM and ML-DSA support aligned with NIST standards. Part of IBM Quantum Safe portfolio.

components.name: Infineon OPTIGA TPM SLB 9672
components.description: Worlds first TPM with PQC-protected firmware using XMSS signatures since 2022.

components.name: Google OpenTitan
components.description: OpenTitan is now shipping in production Chromebooks (announced March 2026) with SLH-DSA secure boot — the first commercially available open-source root-of-trust with PQC secure boot. Second generation will add ML-DSA and ML-KEM. Open-source silicon root-of-trust project led by lowRISC and Google.

components.name: Alpine Linux
components.description: Alpine Linux uses musl libc and is the default base image for millions of Docker containers. Alpine 3.22 ships OpenSSL 3.5.x (edge: 3.5.6), which natively enables NIST PQC (ML-KEM/FIPS203 and ML-DSA/FIPS204) without the separate liboqs-provider package. Alpine's minimal footprint makes PQC library deployment size a consideration. Container workloads using Alpine-based images can inherit hybrid PQC TLS via the built-in OpenSSL provider.

components.name: FreeBSD
components.description: FreeBSD 15.0-RELEASE (Dec 2 2025) ships OpenSSL 3.5.4 LTS with standardized NIST PQC algorithms ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204) and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205), and upgrades OpenSSH to 10.0p2 which enables quantum-resistant hybrid key agreement (e.g. X25519MLKEM768/mlkem768x25519-sha256) by default.

components.name: openSUSE Leap
components.description: openSUSE ships OpenSSL 3.x; Leap 16 is expected to ship OpenSSL 3.5+ enabling PQC by default. Additionally, as of April 2026, openSUSE natively packages libzupt (in both Leap and Tumbleweed) -- a post-quantum SDK providing ML-KEM-768 + X25519 hybrid encryption for files and binary data, with C++/Python/Java bindings (Node.js in development).

components.name: Rocky Linux
components.description: Rocky Linux 10 (RHEL 10 rebuild) already ships OpenSSL 3.5 with full native PQC support (ML-KEM, ML-DSA) as of Rocky Linux 10.1 — the initial 10.0 GA release ran OpenSSL 3.2.2 with PQC available only as a Technology Preview via the third-party oqsprovider package. Rocky Linux 10.1 rebased to OpenSSL 3.5.1, moving PQC algorithms into OpenSSL's native default provider and enabling them in crypto-policies by default. The current release, Rocky Linux 10.2, ships OpenSSL 3.5.5 and adds further PQC coverage: ML-KEM key exchange support for OpenSSH, PQ/T hybrid key exchange in libssh, and PQC definitions in p11-kit's PKCS #11 headers.

components.name: CentOS Stream
components.description: CentOS Stream 10 upstream of RHEL 10. Includes OpenSSL 3.5 with PQC support.

components.name: ChromeOS
components.description: ChromeOS (160M+ devices) inherits hybrid post-quantum TLS 1.3 key exchange from the Chrome browser: the draft Kyber mechanism (X25519Kyber768) was enabled by default from ChromeOS/Chrome 124 (April 2024); it was superseded by the finalized, NIST-standardized ML-KEM-768 (X25519MLKEM768, FIPS 203) as the default from ChromeOS/Chrome 131 (November 2024) — the two codepoints are not wire-compatible. Google's Verified Boot uses SHA-256/RSA for firmware signing — a migration target for ML-DSA. ChromeOS Flex extends PQC TLS to enterprise repurposed hardware. System-level PQC beyond TLS depends on BoringSSL integration.

components.name: NixOS
components.description: NixOS: declarative Linux. Ships latest OpenSSL. When using OpenSSL 3.5+, PQC is available.

components.name: SUSE Linux Enterprise Server (SLES)
components.description: SLES 16.0 has already shipped (GA 4 November 2025 — not 'expected'/future) with OpenSSL 3.5 (native ML-KEM/ML-DSA support); PQC key exchange is enabled by default for SSH per official release notes. SLES 15 SP7 remains on OpenSSL 3.2.3 with limited PQC: a Kyber+classical hybrid TLS key exchange enabled by default since SP6, but no ML-KEM/ML-DSA and no OpenSSL 3.5.

components.name: Arch Linux
components.description: Arch Linux rolling release already ships OpenSSL 3.5+ with PQC support enabled.

components.name: Delinea Secret Server
components.description: Delinea introduced industry-first quantum-safe encryption for Secret Server / Delinea Platform (announced March 2024), leveraging NIST-recommended CRYSTALS-Kyber (Kyber-1024 in place of AES-256 for secret data encryption). The QuantumLock feature (an upgrade of DoubleLock) adds a quantum-resistant layer protecting privileged access to secrets (Kyber/pre-FIPS 203; NIST ML-KEM compliance not confirmed)

components.name: AWS Secrets Manager
components.description: AWS Secrets Manager supports hybrid post-quantum TLS using ML-KEM (Module-Lattice KEM, FIPS 203) combined with classical X25519 for the key exchange on its API endpoints (all Regions except China). An

components.name: Teleport Access Platform
components.description: Teleport: built in Go. Go 1.24+ enables PQC. Teleport v17+ may inherit X25519MLKEM768.

components.name: HashiCorp Boundary
components.description: HashiCorp Boundary is built in Go. Its go.mod (v0.21.3 release tag) declares `go 1.25.7`; CHANGELOG.md confirms this was set in v0.21.1 (2026/02/10): 'Go version bumped to 1.25.7 to address CVE-2025-61730.' Since Go 1.24, the standard library's crypto/tls negotiates the post-quantum hybrid key exchange X25519MLKEM768 by default for TLS 1.3 whenever a module's own go directive is 1.24+ (Boundary's is) and CurvePreferences is not overridden (no such override was found in Boundary's source). This means Boundary's Go-based TLS connections likely negotiate X25519MLKEM768 by default when both peers support it, though HashiCorp has not published documentation describing this as an intentional or supported Boundary feature.

components.name: Cloudflare Zero Trust
components.version: 2026.6.905.0 (Cloudflare One Client, stable, released 2026-08-10) — the Zero Trust platform itself is a SaaS service with no single product version number.
components.description: Cloudflare Zero Trust (formerly Cloudflare Access + Gateway; client renamed from 'WARP' to 'Cloudflare One Client') provides secure web gateway, CASB, and remote access. Cloudflare enabled ML-KEM-768 hybrid TLS 1.3 (X25519MLKEM768) on its global network starting in 2024. The Cloudflare One Client tunnels device traffic via MASQUE over TLS 1.3 with hybrid ML-KEM; Cloudflare Tunnel, IPsec on/off-ramps, and Gateway also support hybrid ML-KEM. As of February 2026, Cloudflare reports 'well over 60%' of human-generated TLS traffic across its global network is protected with hybrid ML-KEM (up from ~33% in March 2025 and 52% by December 2025), making Cloudflare one of the largest real-world PQC deployments.

components.name: Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange
components.description: Zscaler Internet Access (part of the Zero Trust Exchange) performs real-time inline SSL/TLS inspection of PQC traffic, using hybrid post-quantum key exchange built on the NIST-standardized ML-KEM algorithm (FIPS 203) combined with classical ECDHE. PQC negotiation between the client and Zscaler is independent of the destination server's capabilities (Zscaler always offers PQC to the server, but the server decides whether to accept it), giving administrators session-level visibility via logged TLS version and key-exchange group, and protecting the client-to-Zscaler hop against "Harvest Now, Decrypt Later" attacks. Zscaler also supports post-quantum-resistant IPsec VPN tunnels via Pre-Shared, Post-Quantum Keys (PPK, per RFC 8784). Deployment requires no changes to existing customer configurations or hardware.

components.name: Splunk Enterprise
components.description: Splunk Enterprise 10.4 (GA 2026-05-18) adds post-quantum cryptography support in TLS 1.3 connections. Supports ML-KEM (FIPS 203) key-exchange groups: hybrid X25519MLKEM768, SecP256r1MLKEM768, SecP384r1MLKEM1024, and pure MLKEM512/768/1024. Described as the first milestone of phased PQC support (algorithms based on Kyber/Dilithium/SPHINCS+ toward FIPS 203/204/205) (Dilithium referenced; FIPS 204/ML-DSA compliance not confirmed)

components.name: Qualys Cloud Platform
components.description: Qualys CertView (Qualys Cloud Platform) now provides PQC readiness/discovery: detects whether scanned servers support PQC key-exchange (KEM) algorithms via QID 38994, surfacing PQC support status (Supported / Not Supported / Partial Support / Not Applicable) across Monitored, Assets, and Host Instances views. List CertView Certificates API v2.3 adds an instance.PQCSupport filter to query PQC-supported algorithms. This is cryptographic-discovery capability, not PQC implementation in Qualys's own transport.

components.name: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
components.description: AWS IAM is the access control service for all AWS resources. AWS has enabled ML-KEM hybrid TLS 1.3 on the AWS API endpoints and console. As of March 2026, AWS IAM Roles Anywhere supports ML-DSA (FIPS 204) post-quantum digital certificates: ML-DSA-signed CA certificates can be registered as trust anchors, and end-entity certificates bound to ML-DSA-44/65/87 keys can authenticate external workloads via the AWS4-X509-MLDSA signing algorithm to obtain temporary AWS credentials. This is separate from standard IAM/STS SigV4 request signing (using long-term or temporary access keys), which still uses classical HMAC-SHA256 and has no announced ML-DSA migration. AWS Nitro Enclaves and KMS are separate PQC migration targets.

components.name: Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops
components.description: Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops (CVAD) delivers virtualized applications and desktops over the ICA/HDX protocol. All client-server communications use TLS 1.3. CVAD 2507 LTSR's official release notes (initial release and full 'What's new') contain no mention of post-quantum cryptography. PQC capability exists only in the separate NetScaler ADC/Gateway product line (hybrid ML-KEM-768 TLS, GA since NetScaler 14.1-51.72, August 2025), which can front-end CVAD/ICA connections at the TLS layer but does not add PQC to the ICA/HDX protocol channel itself. Citrix has not published a PQC roadmap specific to CVAD or ICA/HDX as of August 2026.

components.name: PuTTY
components.description: PuTTY 0.83 (February 2025) adds ML-KEM support (mlkem768x25519-sha256 hybrid key exchange), which is NIST-standardized (not experimental). NTRU Prime supported since 0.78. Widely deployed in enterprise and government Windows environments.

components.name: AsyncSSH
components.description: AsyncSSH is a Python async SSH library (client and server). Release 2.18.0 (2024-10-26) added post-quantum ML-KEM hybrid key exchange interoperable with OpenSSH 9.9 (mlkem768x25519). sntrup761x25519-sha512@openssh.com supported since 2.12.0 (2022-08-10). ML-KEM is now implemented (not merely planned); as of cryptography 48.0.0, ML-KEM works without liboqs.

components.name: Cisco ASA (Adaptive Security Appliance)
components.description: Per Cisco Secure Firewall PQC roadmap: ASA 9.18+ supports RFC 8784 (PSK mixing in IKEv2); ASA 9.19+ supports RFC 9242 and RFC 9370 hybrid key exchange. ML-KEM support arrives in ASA 9.25 / FTD 10.5 (targeted late 2026); ML-DSA and broader PQC planned for ASA/FTD 11.0 (2H 2027). GA release line is 9.24(x).

components.name: Cisco Meraki MX (Cloud-Managed Firewall)
components.description: Cisco Meraki MX is a cloud-managed next-generation firewall/SD-WAN platform used heavily in branch offices and SMB/enterprise deployments. AutoVPN uses IKEv2/IPsec with classical algorithms. Meraki cloud dashboard communications use TLS 1.3 (classical). New C8455-G2-MX hardware announced as AI/ML and PQC-ready. PQC follows Cisco's quantum-safe roadmap — no specific Meraki firmware PQC timeline published.

components.name: Fortinet FortiGate (FortiOS)
components.description: Fortinet FortiGate is the market-leading enterprise firewall/NGFW. FortiOS 7.6.x supports ML-KEM (Kyber), BIKE, HQC, and Frodo for IPsec key exchange per RFC 9370. FortiOS 8.0 (2026) extends PQC to management and SSL inspection. FortiGate is critical for APAC enterprise and government networks.

components.name: OpenWrt
components.description: OpenWrt: router OS. Ships OpenSSL. PQC available when updated to OpenSSL 3.5+.

components.name: OPNsense
components.description: OPNsense uses LibreSSL/OpenSSL. LibreSSL 4.0+ includes ML-KEM support.

components.name: NGINX Plus
components.description: NGINX Plus R33+ PQC via OQS provider for OpenSSL 3.5.

components.name: Traefik
components.description: Traefik built in Go. Go 1.24+ enables X25519MLKEM768 by default. Traefik v3.3+ inherits PQC.

components.name: Kubernetes
components.description: Since Kubernetes v1.33 (April 2025), the API server and kubelet — built with Go 1.24+ — inherit Go crypto/tls's default hybrid post-quantum key exchange (X25519MLKEM768, combining ML-KEM-768 with classical X25519) for TLS connections, with no explicit Kubernetes configuration required. This covers key exchange only. Kubernetes does not implement or use ML-DSA (FIPS 204) or SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) digital signatures anywhere in the project; PQC signature support is still absent from the Go toolchain Kubernetes depends on (Go's public crypto/mldsa API lands only in Go 1.27, while Kubernetes v1.36 still builds on Go 1.25.x).

components.name: Istio Service Mesh
components.description: Istio adds a Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) option to COMPLIANCE_POLICY since v1.27 (Aug 2025): enforces TLS 1.3, TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256/TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, and post-quantum-safe key exchange X25519MLKEM768 for Envoy/ztunnel mTLS, downstream/upstream TLS, and the Istio xDS server. meshConfig.tlsDefaults.ecdhCurves can be set to X25519MLKEM768.

components.name: Linkerd
components.description: Linkerd defaults to a hybrid ML-KEM-768 + X25519 key exchange (TLS 1.3) for mTLS between meshed pods, introduced in the 2.19 release (Oct 2025) and unchanged as of 2.20 (Jun 2026).

components.name: OpenVPN
components.description: OpenVPN with OpenSSL 3.5 supports ML-KEM/ML-DSA. Hybrid ECDHE-MLKEM deployable.

components.name: Cisco Secure Client (AnyConnect)
components.description: Cisco Secure Client (formerly AnyConnect) is the most widely deployed enterprise VPN client, using SSL/TLS and IKEv2/IPsec for VPN tunnels. Cisco has published a roadmap for its Secure Firewall headend (ASA/FTD): ML-KEM and ML-DSA support for Remote Access VPN targeted for ASA/FTD 11.0 in H2 2027, pending IETF RFC standardization. This roadmap covers the ASA/FTD headend, not the Secure Client application specifically -- Cisco has not published a separate PQC timeline for the Secure Client app itself. Migration will require both client and headend upgrades.

components.name: Apache Traffic Server
components.description: Apache Traffic Server: CDN/proxy. Uses OpenSSL. PQC available with OpenSSL 3.5+.

components.name: libssh
components.description: libssh added native post-quantum hybrid SSH key exchange in release 0.12.0 (2026-02-10). Per the official CHANGELOG: 'Add support for hybrid key exchange mechanisms using Quantum Resistant cryptography for all backends. These are now preferred: sntrup761x25519-sha512, sntrup761x25519-sha512@openssh.com, mlkem768nistp256-sha256, mlkem768x25519-sha256, mlkem1024nistp384-sha384 (only OpenSSL 3.5+ and libgcrypt).' This combines NIST ML-KEM and the NTRU Prime-derived sntrup761 post-quantum KEMs with classical ECDH (Curve25519 or NIST P-256/P-384) into hybrid key-exchange methods negotiated during the SSH transport handshake. This support is exclusive to the 0.12.x release line (latest: 0.12.2, released 2026-07-28); libssh's other maintained branch, 0.11.x (latest: 0.11.5, released 2026-07-21), has received only security backports and does NOT include PQC key exchange.

components.name: Apache Tomcat
components.description: Apache Tomcat: Java web server. Tomcat's TLS connector has native, Tomcat-specific PQC support (not merely inherited from the JDK): its official SSL/TLS Configuration HOW-TO documents a dedicated 'Post Quantum Cryptography' section requiring OpenSSL 3.5+ via the tcnative/FFM OpenSSL provider (which itself needs Java 22+ for the FFM API, not Java 24). SSLHostConfig's <Certificate> element accepts a Tomcat-specific type="MLDSA" value for post-quantum certificate selection at the TLS 1.3 handshake; ML-KEM (e.g. X25519MLKEM768) is negotiated automatically as a TLS key-exchange group by the OpenSSL provider, with no separate Tomcat config keyword.

components.name: Eclipse Jetty
components.description: Eclipse Jetty: Java web server. PQC depends on JDK. Java 24+ has ML-KEM/ML-DSA.

components.name: GitLab CI/CD
components.description: GitLab CI/CD: built partially in Go. gitlab.com servers use PQC TLS from Go 1.24+.

components.name: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect (OIDC)
components.description: Not stated. The document describes standard cryptographic protocols (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, JWT) but contains no mention of Post-Quantum Cryptography algorithms, implementations, or migration plans.

components.name: MySQL Community Server
components.version: LTS: 8.4.11 (2026-07-28); PQC-capable release is the separate Innovation track 26.7.0 (also GA 2026-07-28)
components.description: MySQL: database. Uses OpenSSL for TLS. PQC-capable TLS 1.3 support (hybrid X25519MLKEM768/secp384r1MLKEM1024/secp256r1MLKEM768, pure MLKEM512/768, optional ML-DSA-44/65/87 handshake-signature advertisement via new force_pqc/use_pqc_sign/tls_kex settings) shipped in the MySQL 26.7.0 Innovation release when built against OpenSSL 3.5+. The 8.4.x LTS branch does not yet carry this feature.

components.name: MariaDB Server
components.description: MariaDB: database. Uses OpenSSL/wolfSSL for TLS. PQC available with OpenSSL 3.5+.

components.name: Fireblocks
components.description: Fireblocks research team is mapping candidate PQC signature schemes (ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, FN-DSA plus NIST Round 2 candidates) for its MPC co-signer architecture, and auditing internal crypto infrastructure (certificates, data-at-rest, TLS) for post-quantum readiness. Approach centers on cryptographic agility, threat modeling, and standards engagement; recommends industry quantum readiness by 2030. No production PQC implementation or specific deployed algorithm yet.

components.name: DFNS
components.description: The original document (introducing-hsm, Jul 2025) states the HSM Service offers 'Quantum-safe cryptography support' to future-proof security infrastructure for the post-quantum era, with no algorithms named, framed around the IBM Crypto Express integration. This is no longer the full picture: DFNS's official technical docs (docs.dfns.co, HSM deployment models) list only ECDSA and EdDSA (Ed25519) as supported signature schemes across ALL its HSM integrations (IBM HPCS/EP11, Securosys Primus, Thales Luna, AWS CloudHSM) — no PQC algorithm is listed as supported in production. A newer DFNS blog post ('Securosys HSM Integration', Apr 16 2026) is the first DFNS-published document to name concrete PQC algorithms — ML-DSA, ML-KEM, SLH-DSA — but attributes these explicitly to Securosys's underlying CyberVault hardware generation as a 'post-quantum readiness' capability for future transition, and the same article states DFNS's own HSM integration 'is responsible only for cryptographic operations such as ECDSA (secp256k1) and EdDSA (Ed25519)'. PQC support therefore remains planned/future-facing and is no longer unique to the IBM Crypto Express integration — it now spans DFNS's broader multi-vendor HSM Service (IBM, Securosys, Thales).

components.name: Taurus SA
components.description: Taurus co-leads an open-source post-quantum signature initiative with Project Eleven and Zooko Wilcox (Zcash). It introduced ML-DSA-B, a variant of the NIST standard ML-DSA (FIPS 204) replacing internal hashing with BLAKE3 for up to 60x faster pre-hash, ~20% faster signing, ~30% faster verification. Taurus CSO Jean-Philippe Aumasson co-authored SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) and BLAKE. Forward-looking engineering effort ('cheap insurance policy'), not yet a production custody-signing deployment.

components.name: BitGo
components.description: In May 2026 BitGo, with Silence Laboratories, completed what it describes as the first post-quantum MPC transaction simulation by a regulated custodian, using Silence Labs' PQ-MPC protocol built on ML-DSA (NIST FIPS 204) integrated with BitGo's custody platform. Described as a demonstration/simulation, with continued refinement through select partners rather than immediate production rollout.

components.name: Coinbase Custody
components.description: Coinbase plans to introduce 'quantum-proof' custody services for institutional clients by late 2026, combining existing encryption with emerging NIST-reviewed post-quantum standards (hybrid approach, no single algorithm committed yet). A Coinbase advisory board of cryptographers (convened Jan 2026) published a ~50-page position paper in April 2026 on quantum threats to blockchain; CEO Brian Armstrong also leads an industry coalition pushing Winternitz/BIP-360 for Bitcoin. Building PQ-CoreKMS, a post-quantum version of its CoreKMS Multi-Party Computation (MPC) key-management system that protects approximately 99.9% of custodied assets; plans an automated post-quantum signing pipeline (secure enclaves, secret-sharing, threshold cryptography) within the next year. Coinbase is also a founding member of the Bitcoin Security Consortium (with BlackRock, Fidelity Digital Assets, Block, Blockstream, Strategy) funding Bitcoin post-quantum developer work including BIP-360.

components.name: Bitcoin Core
components.description: Current Bitcoin addresses are not quantum resistant. BIP 360 proposes a "first step" via Pay-to-Merkle-Root (P2MR) to protect against long-exposure attacks by removing keypath spend. The team intends to introduce post-quantum signature schemes for short-exposure protection in future proposals.

components.name: Ethereum (Geth)
components.description: Ethereum has a published quantum-resistance roadmap (ethereum.org/roadmap/future-proofing). It targets: replacing consensus-layer BLS signatures with hash-based Winternitz signatures aggregated via STARKs; moving from KZG commitments to STARK-based data availability; enabling post-quantum user account signatures via native account abstraction (EIP-8141); and migrating ZK proofs from elliptic-curve SNARKs to STARKs. The Ethereum Foundation launched a post-quantum security hub/roadmap in March 2026 with 10+ client teams. Not yet implemented on mainnet.

components.name: Solana
components.description: On 2026-04-27 the Solana Foundation confirmed core teams (Anza and Jump's Firedancer) independently selected Falcon as the network's post-quantum signature scheme (compact signatures), with early implementations already on GitHub. A phased three-step roadmap was published: (1) continue research/evaluate Falcon, (2) adopt PQC for new wallets when quantum becomes a credible threat, (3) migrate existing wallets. Blueshift's Winternitz (WOTS) Vault has been live on mainnet >2 years and was cited by Google Quantum AI as a leading shipped quantum-resistant primitive.

components.name: QRL
components.description: QRL 2.0 / Project Zond Testnet V2 launched 2026-03-31 as an EVM-compatible PoS network. PQC: ML-DSA-87 (CRYSTALS-Dilithium) is the primary signature scheme (mandatory for staking validators, stateless/unlimited signatures) and is fully integrated across the stack; XMSS (stateful, one-time keys) retained from the original 2018 mainnet. SLH-DSA/SPHINCS+ was formally decided on as XMSS's eventual replacement but its implementation has been explicitly rescheduled to post-mainnet — the wallet layer reserves the type but does not yet issue SLH-DSA wallets. ML-KEM is in early-stage development for a future messaging/P2P layer, not yet operational. No official source describes active development of Falcon/FN-DSA; it appears only in a generic future crypto-agility list. The in-house Hyperion compiler lets smart contracts natively verify quantum-secure signatures (ML-DSA-87).

components.name: Algorand
components.description: Algorand has executed the first post-quantum transaction on its mainnet using NIST-selected Falcon signatures (Falcon-1024). The protocol uses Falcon for state proofs every 256 rounds and supports PQC transactions via Logic Signatures. While production-grade code exists, general account and consensus layer integration is described as experimental.

components.name: Cardano
components.description: Input Output Global (IOG) is pursuing post-quantum cryptography (PQC) for Cardano through the 'Cardano Vision 2026' research program (announced 2026-06-19), led by PQC research lead Varun Maram. The program is a phased research roadmap (assessment of PQC building blocks -> design of a post-quantum verifiable random function -> an improved Ouroboros security proof -> a protocol prototype -> eventually a migration-strategy CIP) rather than a committed production rollout with dates. Separately, Cardano Problem Statement CPS-0027 'Approaches to Post-Quantum Signatures' (merged 2026-05-12 into the CIPs repo, status: Open) identifies ML-DSA, Falcon, SLH-DSA, and SQIsign as candidate signature schemes for Plutus but states explicitly that 'the biggest open question is precisely which scheme should be chosen' — no algorithm has been selected and no calendar-dated implementation timeline has been published. No PQC is deployed on the Cardano mainnet.

components.name: IOTA
components.description: IOTA Identity v1.7 (beta, released 2025-10-17) adds NIST-standardized post-quantum signatures: ML-DSA (security levels 44, 65, 87), SLH-DSA (128/192/256), and FALCON (512/1024), plus hybrid composite signatures id-MLDSA44-Ed25519 and id-MLDSA65-Ed25519 for Verifiable Credentials. Currently an experimental feature for developers (dependent on key-storage support). (Legacy Tangle used Winternitz OTS.)

components.name: Cosmos/Tendermint
components.description: Cosmos SDK v0.55.0 (released 2026-07-27, requires CometBFT v0.40.0) shipped official NIST ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) post-quantum signature support: PR #26436 added ML-DSA-65 as a validator consensus key type with SDK key wrappers, Amino/interface-registry registration, and multisig support; PR #26472 added ML-DSA-65 support for user account keys (mnemonic keyring creation via --algo ml_dsa_65, tx signing/verification); PR #26614 extended support to the enterprise PoA module. Adoption is opt-in: existing chains default to genesis.consensus_params.validator.pub_key_types=["ed25519"] and must explicitly add ml_dsa_65 (plus validator key rotation) to enable it; new chains can set it directly. This is the official Cosmos SDK/CometBFT team's own work and is distinct from DoraFactory/pqc-cosmos, an unaffiliated third-party hackathon project (MIT iQuHack 2025, dormant since Feb 2025) with no relationship to the Interchain Foundation, Cosmos SDK team, or CometBFT.

components.name: Aptos
components.description: AIP-137 (Accepted status as of 2026-04-07, promoted from Draft; last call ended 02/09/2026) adds optional SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s (FIPS 205) signatures for Aptos accounts. Implementation is partially merged into aptos-core: aptos-crypto library support (PR #18293, merged 2025-12-10) and the transaction authenticator (PR #18300, merged 2026-01-15). TS SDK support and gas pricing are also complete per the AIP's own milestone checklist; CLI support, indexer support, and developer documentation remain pending. Implementation details: 48-byte secret keys, 32-byte public keys, 7,856-byte signatures (82x larger than Ed25519). Benchmarks show verification is ~5x slower than Ed25519 (294µs vs 60µs, x86_64). No mainnet or devnet deployment has occurred; the AIP targets only a non-binding 'preliminary devnet deployment early [2026]' with explicit no urgency for mainnet. Future support for ML-DSA and Falcon is mentioned as potential alternatives but not currently implemented.

components.name: Avalanche
components.description: Proposal for a staged transition using a Hybrid Signature Model combining ECDSA with Falcon/Dilithium. Includes C-Chain precompiles for PQC verification and Subnet Modularity for testing PQ-only environments before mainnet enforcement. Currently in technical review phase via ACP repository.

components.name: Sui
components.description: Sui/Mysten Labs has announced a concrete PQC implementation timeline (blog post 'Making Sui Quantum Ready', published Aug 6, 2026): quantum-safe SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s (FIPS 205) vaults for Move smart contracts are targeted for Mainnet in 2026; native ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) account support is targeted for Testnet by end of 2026, with Mainnet native account authentication targeted for Q1 2027. Sui's deterministic key derivation lets users move to a quantum-safe key using their existing recovery phrase, and ML-DSA-65 will be supported in Sui's multisig authenticator. Mysten Labs explicitly states this 'reflects current direction, not a finished, fully audited release' and that 'timelines are kept open while independent review continues.'

components.name: Broadcom Avi (NSX ALB)
components.description: Application delivery controller and load balancer (formerly Avi Networks / VMware NSX ALB) with L4-L7 load balancing, WAF, and service mesh integration. Version 31.2.1 ships GA PQC: pure ML-KEM, hybrid KEMs, and ML-DSA for TLS 1.3. Note: not supported with Intel QAT or FIPS-enabled deployments.

components.name: Fortinet FortiGate-Rugged
components.description: FortiOS 7.6+ includes PQC (ML-KEM, BIKE, HQC, Frodo). Applies to all FortiGate models.

components.name: evolutionQ BasejumpQDN
