components.description: Software platform for building a Quantum Delivery Network (QDN) that unifies Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) in a single control plane. Each BasejumpQDN node runs a crypto-agile key agent that delivers QKD-derived keys, PQC-derived keys (ML-KEM for key establishment, ML-DSA for authentication), or Multimodal hybrid keys (QKD + PQC + symmetric), with automatic fallback to PQC/hybrid key establishment if the QKD key supply is interrupted. Extends key delivery across fiber distances beyond QKD's natural range limit using trusted repeater nodes (evolutionQ's product page states 'a few hundred kilometers'; a 2025 evolutionQ/Nokia joint paper cites '~100-125 km' for current QKD technology — no evolutionQ source states '~300 km'). Vendor-neutral — validated with over 10 QKD vendors via ETSI GS QKD 014, including ID Quantique and Toshiba by name, preventing lock-in. Includes BasejumpSIM cloud-based simulation tool for modeling QDN deployments before physical rollout. Used by Nokia and ID Quantique in a live network trial for Proximus (Belgian telecom) — 'Europe's first live hybrid quantum encryption key trial,' completed June 2023 between Brussels and Mechelen; both evolutionQ and ID Quantique describe this as a trial/demonstration, not an ongoing production deployment.

components.name: evolutionQ BasejumpSKI
components.description: Symmetric Key Infrastructure (SKI) combining symmetric pre-shared keys (PSK), classical ECDH, and NIST-approved post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM) in evolutionQ's Multimodal key establishment protocol (Key = KDF(ECDH, ML-KEM, symmetric key share)). Delivers hybrid quantum-safe end-to-end encryption keys without requiring QKD hardware or significant infrastructure changes; the product is explicitly 'Upgradeable to support Quantum Networks: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD)' as an optional future path, not a bundled feature. Designed as a drop-in complement to BasejumpQDN for organizations in early PQC migration stages or those not yet deploying QKD hardware.

components.name: Qrypt BLAST SDK
components.description: REST API and SDK implementing the BLAST algorithm for generating identical symmetric encryption keys independently at multiple endpoints — without transmitting keys over the network. Eliminates the key distribution problem. Powered by quantum entropy sourced from ICFO (Spain), Los Alamos National Lab, Oak Ridge National Lab, and EPFL (Switzerland). Peer-reviewed algorithm (Prof. Yevgeniy Dodis, NYU). Available as cloud API and on-premises. AWS Marketplace listed. Partnership with Fortanix for multi-source quantum entropy compliance (March 2026). Note: ML-KEM/Kyber is used by a separate Qrypt product (the NVIDIA Quantum Secure Gateway IPsec/IKEv2 plugin, which combines PQC algorithms with BLAST as two distinct successive key-exchange stages under RFC 9370) — it is not part of this SDK's own technical approach.

components.name: ISARA Advance
components.description: Autonomous cryptographic inventory and risk assessment tool from ISARA Corporation. Continuously catalogs and monitors cryptographic assets across environments — algorithms, protocols, devices, certificates, and keys. Provides risk-prioritized migration roadmap for transitioning to post-quantum cryptography. Designed as a companion discovery tool to ISARA Radiate (PQC algorithm library), enabling organizations to assess their cryptographic exposure before beginning PQC remediation. Supports enterprise-wide CBOM generation and compliance gap analysis.

components.name: 1Password
components.description: 1Password deployed hybrid post-quantum key exchange (X25519MLKEM768) for all 1Password web application TLS connections, announced 2026-03-31. Combines classical X25519 with ML-KEM-768; protects against harvest-now-decrypt-later. Works automatically in compatible browsers (Chrome, Firefox) with no config or performance penalty. This is phase one of a broader roadmap to expand PQC coverage across products.

components.name: Gmail / Google Workspace
components.description: Google's cloud email and productivity platform. Transport layer protected by ML-KEM hybrid TLS via BoringSSL on Google's servers — HNDL-resistant for email in transit since 2024. S/MIME end-to-end encryption uses classical RSA/ECDSA certificates with no PQC S/MIME certificate issuance available. Google Workspace Client-Side Encryption (CSE) uses classical ECDH key wrapping. Full PQC for message content depends on PKI ecosystem and S/MIME standards maturity.

components.name: WhatsApp
components.description: WhatsApp's current official technical documentation (Encryption Overview whitepaper v9, Feb 25 2026) describes only the classical Signal Protocol key exchange (Curve25519 prekey bundle + Double Ratchet); it contains no reference to post-quantum cryptography. PQXDH with ML-KEM-1024 is documented by Signal (signal.org), a separate company/app from WhatsApp/Meta, and no WhatsApp-specific source confirms this has shipped to WhatsApp users.

components.name: VIAVI TeraVM Security Test
components.description: Cloud-enabled platform for benchmarking enterprise VPN gateways and IPSec systems migrating to NIST PQC algorithms. Security Test module emulates tens of thousands of concurrent users with realistic application traffic while measuring PQC-specific KPIs: handshake latency, SA establishment time, re-keying overhead, key size impact. Supports hybrid IKEv2 key exchange (RFC 9370, RFC 9242) and Post-Quantum Preshared Key (RFC 8784) to validate backward compatibility. Partnership with QNu Labs (announced Dec 4, 2025) for QKD/QRNG/hybrid PQC test-case definition and badging. The widely-cited 'IKEv2 SA establishment increases from 38ms (classical) to 12,626ms' figure is NOT a VIAVI/TeraVM benchmark result — it is a third-party case-study figure from Banco Santander (presented by Jaime Gomez Garcia at the ETSI Quantum Safe Cryptography Conference), merely reported in a July 2025 VIAVI Perspectives blog post; it should not be presented as a TeraVM 'key finding.' VIAVI's current TeraVM Security data sheet (rev. 0925, Sept 2025) explicitly names the final NIST standard — 'PQC ML-KEM (FIPS-203)' — so VIAVI's live documentation has moved past draft-era naming.

components.name: Keysight CyPerf
components.description: Cloud-native network security test platform validating hybrid post-quantum TLS 1.3 handshakes using X25519+ML-KEM-768 across distributed physical and cloud environments. Version 7.0.2 (Oct 2025) supports hybrid key exchange simulation with Cloudflare endpoint. Stateful traffic generation at 1; 10; 100; 400 Gbps. Community Edition available free. Integrates with BreakingPoint System via ATI-2025-15 application for hybrid PQC encrypted traffic simulation in security appliance testing.

components.name: Keysight Inspector
components.description: Device security testing platform (via Riscure acquisition) using the Crypto 3 modular framework for PQC side-channel and fault-injection testing. Dedicated Correlation Power Analysis (CPA) acquisition/analysis workflows evaluate ML-KEM-512/768/1024 side-channel resistance; ML-DSA/Dilithium testing is framed under the Crypto 3 framework. Collaborated with NXP on ML-DSA countermeasure validation and PQShield on industry readiness.

components.name: CryptoNext COMPASS Network Probe
components.description: Passive high-performance cryptographic data detection system deploying on network taps and SPAN ports. Identifies all cryptographic algorithms; key types; and certificate details across 100+ IT and OT protocols in real time without packet injection. First EU company to achieve NIST CAVP certification for all three finalized PQC algorithms (ML-KEM/FIPS 203; ML-DSA/FIPS 204; SLH-DSA/FIPS 205) in June 2025. On path to FIPS 140-3 module certification. Integrates with COMPASS Analytics Platform for governance reporting. Recommended by NIST NCCoE for cryptographic discovery in PQC migration workflows. Secure boot; hardened OS; integrity checks; PQC-secured TLS 1.3 management communications.

properties.name: pqctoday:fips_validated
properties.value: Partial (NIST CAVP certified; FIPS 140-3 in progress)

components.name: pqcscan
components.description: Open-source PQC readiness scanner written in Rust. Two scan modes: tls-scan (probes HTTPS/TLS endpoints for standardized PQC/hybrid key-exchange groups using final NIST names — e.g. X25519MLKEM768, SECP384R1MLKEM1024, MLKEM768, MLKEM1024 — plus TLS version and cipher suite) and ssh-scan (probes SSH servers for PQC key-exchange (KEM) algorithm support, e.g. ml-kem-*, sntrup761x25519-*, mlkem768x25519-*; the server's host-key/signature algorithm list is captured and reported but is NOT classified against a PQC signature database — the tool currently ships no ML-DSA/SLH-DSA/Dilithium/SPHINCS+ list for SSH host keys or TLS signature schemes). Algorithm matching is done by name against bundled JSON tables (kex_algos.json, tls_groups.json, tls_cipher_suites.json, tls_sig_schemes.json), not by OID. Outputs JSON with HTML report generation. Binary releases for Linux, macOS, Windows. Developed by Anvil Secure. Both released versions (0.7.0, released 2025-07-02; 0.8.0, released 2025-11-08) postdate FIPS 203/204/205 finalization (Aug 2024) and use final NIST algorithm names.

components.name: pqc-flow
components.version: No tagged release — unversioned (pre-1.0, main branch only)
components.description: Detects PQC and hybrid algorithm usage in live network traffic and PCAP captures. SSH detection (production): sntrup761x25519-sha512@openssh.com (OpenSSH 9.0+) via custom SSH_MSG_KEXINIT parser; mlkem/kyber/ntruprime SSH variants are pattern-ready but NOT yet implemented (roadmap item). TLS 1.3 detection: X25519Kyber768 (Chrome 0x11ec), X25519Kyber768Draft00 (Cloudflare 0xfe31/0x6399), NIST ML-KEM drafts (0x2001+) via custom ClientHello/ServerHello supported_groups and key_share extension parser. QUIC detection via TLS-in-QUIC handshake parsing. IKE/IPsec via nDPI classification (limited metadata support, not extensively tested). Post-quantum signature detection (ML-DSA/Dilithium, SLH-DSA/SPHINCS+, Falcon) is roadmap-only, not yet implemented — requires future TLS certificate parsing. PQC flags bitmask tracks KEM presence, signature presence, hybrid negotiation, offered-only, and session resumption states. No nDPI patches required for SSH/TLS PQC extraction.

components.name: PQC-LEO
components.description: Open-source PQC benchmarking and evaluation framework automating computational and network performance measurement for NIST PQC algorithms. Uses OpenSSL with OQS provider to run standardized TLS 1.3 performance tests across x86 and ARM architectures. Measures: handshake latency; key generation time; signing/verification overhead; memory footprint; energy consumption. Generates comparative analysis between classical; hybrid; and pure PQC configurations. Designed for academic research and enterprise pre-deployment evaluation. [Note: release date predates FIPS 203/204/205 finalization (Aug 2024); may reference draft/pre-standard algorithms.]

components.name: Q-CORE Q-Scanner
components.description: Free PQC/TLS vulnerability audit tool: scans a domain's TLS configuration (all TLS versions, cipher suites, certificate chain, HTTP security headers) and quantum-risk-scores it; detects ML-KEM (Kyber), ML-DSA (Dilithium), and other NIST post-quantum standards present in the handshake (9 scan areas, 117 tests, per qcore.systems). Bundled free into every tier of the wider Q-CORE Systems s.r.o. platform (220+ modules as of Aug 2026). Higher paid tiers/modules — not Q-Scanner itself — separately claim a broader PQC algorithm portfolio (Business tier: 19 PQC algorithms incl. ML-DSA, ML-KEM, SLH-DSA, FALCON, HQC, BIKE, NTRU, MAYO, CROSS, UOV, SNoVA, delivered via modules such as Q-SHIELD/Q-SIGN).

components.name: PQCryptoLib-Core
components.description: FIPS 140-3 certified cryptographic library from PQShield supporting all NIST-standardized PQC algorithms: ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), SLH-DSA (FIPS 205), plus hash-based LMS and XMSS and Falcon. OpenSSL integration via provider. CMVP certificate #4800 is Level 1 (not Level 3), validated 2024-09-16 for PQCryptoLib v1.0.0 covering classical algorithms only (no PQC in validated scope). ACVP certs: A3011 (v1.0.0), A7693 (v1.0.2), A6553 (v3.0.0). PQC-inclusive CMVP module (with ML-KEM/ML-DSA) on the NIST Modules-in-Process/IUT list. Targets enterprise and government deployments.

properties.name: pqctoday:fips_validated
properties.value: Yes (FIPS 140-3 CMVP #4800, Level 1, validated 2024-09-16, classical algorithms only; PQC not in FIPS scope). PQC CMVP (ML-KEM/ML-DSA) in process; CAVP A7693 (v1.0.2) and A6553 (v3.0.0)

components.name: PQMicroLib-Core
components.description: Embedded-optimized PQC cryptographic library from PQShield targeting ARM and RISC-V microcontrollers. Implements ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), SLH-DSA (FIPS 205), LMS, and XMSS. Implements the PSA Certified Crypto API (listed in the official PSA Certified product directory as a Crypto API integration/conformance listing, not a tiered PSA Certified product security certification) and integrates with Mbed TLS and the PSA Cryptography framework. CAVP-Ready (inherits algorithms from CAVP-certified PQCryptoLib-Core but has not undergone independent CAVP validation). FIPS 140-3 CMVP module in process. Designed for resource-constrained IoT, automotive, and industrial embedded systems.

properties.name: pqctoday:fips_validated
properties.value: Partial (CAVP-Ready via PQCryptoLib-Core; CMVP in process)

components.name: Crucible
components.version: Unversioned (no GitHub releases or tags exist; project tracks the main branch)
components.description: Conformance testing harness for ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and ML-DSA (FIPS 204) cryptographic library implementations. Tests real-world vulnerabilities that evade both NIST Known Answer Tests and formal verification tools. ML-KEM: 78 tests across 6 categories (compression algorithms; NTT operations; coefficient bounds validation; decapsulation logic; serialization; sampling distributions). ML-DSA: 51 tests across 6 categories (norm checks; arithmetic operations; signing determinism; verification robustness; serialization; timing consistency). Uses a language-agnostic JSON line protocol enabling harness support for C; C++; Go; Java; Rust; and other languages. Ships with harnesses for 19 production implementations across 7 languages including CIRCL; liboqs; AWS-LC; Go stdlib; and Bouncy Castle. Created by Symbolic Software.

components.name: Xiphera PQC IP Cores
components.description: xQlave® is Xiphera's family of FPGA/ASIC IP cores for post-quantum cryptography, implemented purely in digital logic (no embedded CPU or software). The family includes at least two distinct cores confirmed via Xiphera's own product briefs: XIP6110B, a Balanced ML-KEM 512/768/1024 Key Encapsulation IP core compliant with FIPS 203 (product brief ver. 1.2.0, 2025-02-13); and XIP6220B, a Balanced ML-DSA-44/65/87 Digital Signature IP core supporting hedged, deterministic, and pre-hash variants, compliant with FIPS 204 (product brief ver. 1.1.2, 2025-11-18). Both cores use a simple 64-bit interface for integration, are constant-time/side-channel resistant, and perform a few thousand operations per second in a typical FPGA implementation. Vendor: Xiphera Ltd., Espoo, Finland.

components.name: Kudelski IoT Security Platform
components.description: Post-quantum support lives specifically in Kudelski Secure Enclave (KSE), a silicon-proven, modular hardware Root of Trust IP for semiconductor/SoC designs (KSE2/KSE3/KSE5 family) that embeds NIST-selected ML-KEM and ML-DSA algorithms with side-channel and fault countermeasures, for PQC-ready secure boot, secure update, key management, and provisioning. This is distinct from Kudelski's companion device-lifecycle-management product, keySTREAM, which handles quantum-safe credential provisioning and firmware-update management across the device lifecycle (manufacturing through decommissioning) but does not itself implement the PQC algorithms.

components.name: Cisco IOS XR
components.description: Cisco IOS XR is the service-provider routing OS for ASR 9000, NCS, and 8000 platforms. Separately from the ML-KEM/ML-DSA (NIST-PQC) roadmap, which is not yet GA, IOS XR has shipped a distinct quantum-safe mechanism since Release 24.1.1 on the Cisco NCS 1004 optical platform: RFC 8784 Postquantum Preshared Keys (PPK) for IKEv2/OTNsec encryption, available as manual PPK or dynamic PPK via the Cisco Secure Key Integration Protocol (SKIP) against an external key source (e.g. QKD). This is a symmetric-key-based quantum-resistance method, not a NIST ML-KEM/ML-DSA lattice algorithm. Full IOS XR NIST-PQC (ML-KEM/ML-DSA) migration is expected to follow the IOS XE 26 roadmap; not yet formally announced as of Q1 2026.

components.name: Cisco Catalyst Center
components.description: Cisco Catalyst Center (formerly DNA Center) is the enterprise campus network management and intent-based networking platform. Its own management-channel TLS (northbound API, GUI, device communication) currently supports only RSA and ECDSA identity certificates per the official Administrator Guide (Release 3.2.x); no PQC/ML-KEM capability is documented for Catalyst Center itself as of its latest release (3.2.3, Jul 2026). PQC MACsec and IKEv2 ML-KEM orchestration for Cisco 8000 Series routers/DMVPN/FlexVPN is a documented capability of the separate 'Catalyst Manager' (Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, formerly vManage) product, not Catalyst Center — these are distinct Cisco products with similar names.

components.name: Red Hat OpenShift
components.description: OpenShift Container Platform 4.22 bundles Kubernetes 1.35 (confirmed 'This release uses Kubernetes 1.35 with CRI-O runtime,' RHEA-2026:0449). Per Red Hat's official 4.22 release notes ('About PQC compliance'), OpenShift supports PQC readiness for secure cluster communication via RHEL/RHCOS platform cryptographic capabilities and TLS 1.3 security profiles, including hybrid ML-KEM key exchange where enabled by the configured TLS profile and supported by the component — inherited from the underlying platform/Kubernetes stack, not an OpenShift-specific algorithm addition. Only ML-KEM is documented (no ML-DSA/SLH-DSA in base OpenShift release notes).

properties.name: pqctoday:fips_validated
properties.value: Partial (RHEL FIPS module; PQC not in FIPS module)

components.name: DigiCert CertCentral
components.description: CertCentral does not currently issue PQC certificates. DigiCert's own current documentation states: 'At the current time, CertCentral doesn't issue public CA certificates with these algorithms' (ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, ML-KEM). DigiCert's PQC-support matrix lists Private CA, Device Trust, Document Trust, Software Trust, TrustCore SDK, TrustEdge, and Trust Lifecycle Manager as PQC-capable services; CertCentral is not included. No CertCentral-specific PQC timeline or committed date was found in any DigiCert source. The previously-cited 'Early enterprise pilots' / 'PQC Labs adoption' / 2025-2026 language originates from DigiCert's generic, company-wide marketing guide, which never mentions CertCentral by name.

components.name: DigiCert ONE
components.description: DigiCert ONE's core platform services (Private CA, Trust Lifecycle Manager, Software Trust Manager, Device Trust Manager, Document Trust Manager) support NIST-standardized ML-DSA (signatures) and SLH-DSA (long-lived signature use cases). ML-KEM (key encapsulation) is NOT yet supported by these core services — per DigiCert's own PQC compatibility documentation, ML-KEM is available only in TrustCore SDK and TrustEdge, separate open-source embedded-device SDK/agent products that integrate with the platform rather than the core PKI services. Offers cryptographic agility, lifecycle automation, and developer tools. Industry leaders are using PQC in production via DigiCert.

components.name: Crypto4A QxEDGE
components.description: Crypto4A QxEDGE is a hyper-converged Hardware Security Platform (HSP) combining a quantum-safe, crypto-agile HSM with confidential-compute processing, deployable at the edge or in the data center for hosting security applications such as PKI, code signing, and key management. Official positioning (crypto4a.com meta description): 'QxEDGE combines quantum-safe HSM, confidential compute, and multi-tenant processing to deliver secure, programmable edge infrastructure.' It is not marketed specifically as a resource-constrained or air-gapped-only IoT/OT appliance. Supports ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, XMSS, and LMS via its QASM cryptographic core.

components.name: IBM z/OS Cryptographic Services (ICSF)
components.description: IBM z/OS ICSF (Integrated Cryptographic Service Facility) provides quantum-safe cryptography on IBM Z hardware (z16+). Supports ML-KEM and ML-DSA via z/OS V2.5+ with hardware acceleration through the IBM Crypto Express 8S adapter. Provides quantum-safe API functions for application programs, migrating from Dilithium/Kyber to ML-DSA/ML-KEM per NIST FIPS 203/204. Part of IBM's quantum-safe z/OS infrastructure.

components.name: IBM MQ
components.version: 10.0.0.0 (LTS, GA 16 June 2026; 19 June 2026 for MQ for z/OS)
components.description: From IBM MQ 10.0 (GA 16 June 2026), quantum-safe TLS key exchange using FIPS 203 ML-KEM and Hybrid ML-KEM is supported on AIX, Linux, and Windows queue managers and C clients, configured via the SSLQS/SSLQSR channel attributes, protecting against 'harvest now, decrypt later' attacks. Per IBM's own documentation, ML-DSA support is NOT available in IBM MQ Advanced Message Security ('Currently, there is no support for the quantum safe algorithms available within Advanced Message Security'), and the quantum-safe TLS feature is not documented as available for IBM MQ for z/OS.

components.name: Palo Alto Prisma SASE
components.description: Quantum-Safe Security (Strata Cloud Manager app) reached GA Jan 30, 2026, covering NGFW and Prisma Access; ML-KEM support delivered via Cipher Translation re-encryption at the network edge.

components.name: Sectigo Certificate Manager (SCM)
components.description: Sectigo Certificate Manager (SCM) is the enterprise CLM platform for TLS, S/MIME, code signing, and IoT certificates. On 14 April 2026 Sectigo launched Private PQC built into SCM: eligible SCM Private CA customers can issue and manage private-only (not public-trust) PQC certificates — SSL/TLS, Code Signing, Client/S-MIME, and Device (Server Auth & Client Auth) — using ML-DSA (ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, ML-DSA-87) via familiar SCM workflows, hosted by Sectigo and backed by a Sectigo-operated Private CA and virtual HSM. Certificates have one-year lifetimes and are explicitly not production-ready by design (experimental/evaluation use).

components.name: Fortinet FortiWeb
components.description: FortiWeb 8.0.3 (December 2025) introduces PQC in TLS 1.3 via OpenSSL 3.5: ML-KEM key exchange groups (mlkem512/mlkem768/mlkem1024) plus hybrid ECC-PQC modes and ML-DSA signature algorithms. CLI-configurable for both client-side server policies and server pool connections.

components.name: SEALSQ QS7001
components.description: Supports Post Quantum Cryptography algorithms: Crystal Kyber (KEM) and Crystal Dilithium (Signature). Features a dedicated ad-X4 hardware cryptographic accelerator for fast encryption/authentication including PQC acceleration (Kyber/Dilithium per SEALSQ datasheets; NIST FIPS 203/204 compliance not confirmed)

components.name: Microchip PolarFire
components.description: PolarFire 'S' FPGAs' dedicated hardware crypto processor is CAVP-validated for classical algorithms only (AES, SHA, HMAC, ECDSA, RSA, DSA, DRBG) — the current official Security User Guide never mentions ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA/LMS/XMSS or any FIPS 203/204/205 algorithm. Real PQC support (FIPS 203/204/205) instead comes from separate third-party IP cores synthesized into the FPGA's reconfigurable logic fabric, alongside/instead of the built-in processor.

components.name: PQShield Core
components.description: Provides latest NIST-standardized post-quantum and PQ/T Hybrid algorithms in a software environment. Optimized for crypto-agility and FIPS-compliant PQ/T Hybrid solutions to protect against 'Harvest Now Decrypt Later' attacks. Supports smooth transition to quantum resistance.

components.name: IBM Guardium Safe
components.description: IBM Guardium Quantum Safe (also branded IBM Guardium Cryptography Manager) lets organizations assess post-quantum cryptography risk, discover cryptographic artifacts/vulnerabilities, generate a Cryptography Bill of Materials (CBOM), flag outdated/vulnerable algorithms, enforce policy, and produce audit-ready reports. Actively maintained through 2026.

components.name: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
components.description: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS 'Resolute Raccoon' (released 23 April 2026) ships OpenSSL 3.5 with NIST PQC algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) enabled by default, and OpenSSH 10.2p1 with hybrid post-quantum key exchange mlkem768x25519-sha256 (ML-KEM-768 + X25519) as the default; legacy DSA host keys/auth removed.

components.name: STMicroelectronics ST33KTPM
components.description: ST33KTPM is STMicroelectronics' STSAFE-TPM 2.0 product series (TCG TPM 2.0-compliant discrete TPM), sold in three variants for computers/servers, embedded systems, and industrial systems; the flagship, fully-documented SKU is ST33KTPM2X. The quantum-resistant feature that ships TODAY is a PQC-protected firmware-update mechanism, not a general PQC crypto engine: firmware images are dual-signed with ECDSA (NIST P-384) and an LMS hash-based signature (NIST SP 800-208), and the device keeps a redundant second firmware image with automatic fail-over/autorepair if an update is interrupted or corrupted — this fault-tolerant dual-image design is the real basis for the 'dual firmware' marketing language. ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and ML-DSA (FIPS 204) are NOT active/shipping algorithms on the device today. ST's own product campaign page states this LMS-protected update channel merely 'enables existing products to support additional post-quantum cryptographic algorithms, such as ML-KEM and ML-DSA, through field firmware upgrades' — i.e. a roadmap capability delivered via a not-yet-published future firmware update, not a currently implemented one. The live ST33KTPM2X data brief (STMicroelectronics doc DB5174, Rev 3, May 2025) lists only classical algorithms today (RSA up to 4096-bit, ECC/ECDSA/ECDH/ECSchnorr/ECDAA, AES-128/192/256, SHA-1/2/3, HMAC) plus the LMS firmware-signing mechanism, and contains zero mentions of ML-KEM or ML-DSA anywhere in its 25 pages.

components.name: IDEMIA PQC Accelerator
components.description: Hardware accelerator utilizing Keccak to offload intensive tasks from the main processor. Optimizes performance for quantum-resistant algorithms standardized by NIST: ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205). Designed for seamless transition without compromising speed.

components.name: Adva FSP 3000 S-Flex
components.description: The solution delivers quantum-safe Layer 1 encryption utilizing post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and post-quantum key exchange. It is approved by the German Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) for VS-NfD and EU/NATO-restricted data, protecting against harvest-now, decrypt-later attacks.

components.name: CryptoNext COMPASS Probe
components.description: The product features enhanced security with encrypted communications using post-quantum TLS 1.3. It is part of a suite designed to help organizations map assets and prepare for PQC migration, but the probe itself primarily detects existing protocols rather than implementing PQC algorithms for data protection beyond its own management interface.

components.name: Citrix CVAD
components.description: Citrix: Virtual Apps & Desktops Security Baseline

components.name: Zscaler ZTE
components.description: Zscaler Internet Access (part of the Zero Trust Exchange/ZTE) provides real-time inline inspection of PQC traffic via hybrid PQC key exchange in TLS 1.2/1.3, auto-detecting ML-KEM (FIPS 203, finalized August 2024) and Open Quantum Safe groups alongside classical elliptic curves. This PQC negotiation between the client and Zscaler is independent of the destination server's capabilities — Zscaler always offers PQC to the server, but the client-to-Zscaler leg is protected from 'Harvest Now, Decrypt Later' attacks regardless of whether the server supports PQC. Supports IPsec with Pre-shared Post-Quantum Keys (PPK) per RFC 8784 to protect IKE key derivation against quantum attacks without requiring full PQC algorithms in the exchange.

components.name: Akamai Edge
components.description: Supports ML-KEM based hybrid key exchange (X25519MLKEM768, per NIST FIPS 203) for TLS 1.3, via two separate Property Manager behaviors: 'PQC Client to Edge' and 'PQC to Origin.' PQC Client to Edge is now enabled BY DEFAULT for all Enhanced TLS hostnames (techdocs last modified 2026-08-10) — the original 'limited availability, contact your Akamai representative' framing now applies only to Standard TLS hostnames.

components.name: JetBrains TeamCity 2026.1
components.description: JetBrains TeamCity: CI/CD, Java-based. Starting with TeamCity 2026.1, the SERVER supports only Java 21 (build agents support Java 21 through 25). Because ML-KEM/ML-DSA landed as standard JDK features only in Java 24 (JEP 496/497), the TeamCity server's Java-21-only requirement means the server process itself has no path to native JVM PQC support under 2026.1; a build agent running under JDK 24+ could access JVM-level PQC APIs for build-time crypto operations, but that is agent-side only, not server-side.

components.name: Keyfactor 2026 Trends
components.description: The document states Keyfactor is a leader in "post-quantum readiness" and predicts vendors will release products with PQC capabilities in 2026. It mentions a "PQC Lab" sandbox for getting quantum-ready but does not explicitly state that the core production platform currently supports specific PQC algorithms or hybrid modes.

components.name: AppViewX Spring 2026
components.description: The Spring 2026 release expands cryptographic visibility to support post-quantum cryptography (PQC) initiatives through enhanced agentless discovery of certificates and cipher usage. It enables planning for PQC readiness and modernization but does not explicitly state the implementation of specific PQC algorithms or production support yet.

components.name: Sectigo 2026 Predictions
components.description: The document is a prediction article, not a product specification. It states that 2026 will be the year of PQC execution with pilot rollouts and automation. It mentions NIST finalizing foundational standards in 2024 and expects formal definitions for PQC versions of major certificate types by end of 2026. No specific algorithms or implementation details for Sectigo products are provided.

components.name: Entrust Cryptographic Platform
components.description: The platform advances full-stack PQC readiness through expansion announced in February 2026. It integrates hardware security modules, PKI, certificate life-cycle management, discovery, and compliance governance to support enterprise quantum preparedness and crypto-agility. Specific algorithms are not listed.

components.name: Venafi TLS PQC Continuity
components.description: This is an Internet-Draft proposing a TLS extension (`pq_cert_available`) to prevent downgrade attacks during PQC migration. It allows clients to cache server commitments to use PQC algorithms (specifically referencing ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, and composites). It is not a software product but a protocol specification under development.

components.name: Sectigo Cert Manager 2026
components.description: Sectigo launched Private PQC built into Sectigo Certificate Manager (SCM) on 2026-04-14, enabling enterprises to issue and manage private PQC SSL/TLS certificates in existing SCM workflows. Supports ML-DSA (Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm) variants ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87 (FIPS 204; X.509 usage per RFC 9881). Available to existing Sectigo Private CA customers on request.

components.name: Xiphera XIP6110B
components.description: IP core implementing ML-KEM (formerly CRYSTALS-Kyber) key generation, encapsulation, and decapsulation for all ML-KEM-512/768/1024 variants; compliant with NIST FIPS 203. Hardware-only implementation (no software components) with constant-time execution for protection against timing side-channel attacks. Member of the Xiphera xQlave PQC IP core family.

components.name: A10 Networks Thunder ADC
components.description: A10 introduced hybrid post-quantum KEM support in the Thunder SSL/TLS data plane in ACOS 7.0.3 (built on OpenSSL 3.5). Supported hybrid key-exchange groups: X25519+ML-KEM-768, secp256r1+ML-KEM-768, and secp384r1+ML-KEM-1024, combining classical ECDHE with ML-KEM so both must be broken to compromise a session. Delivered via software update, no new hardware required.

components.name: Citrix ADC (NetScaler)
components.description: Production-ready, NIST-aligned hybrid post-quantum cryptography using X25519 + ML-KEM768. Provides forward-looking protection and backward compatibility. Available now for external-facing services.

components.name: Lattice MachXO5-NX
components.description: Supports CNSA 2.0-required and NIST-approved PQC algorithms (LMS, XMSS, ML-DSA, ML-KEM; SLH-DSA claimed in marketing copy only, not in the per-device technical comparison table). PQC services available only in TDQ devices — and vary by device size: the largest device (LFMXO5-55TDQ) gets the full ML-DSA/ML-KEM/XMSS/LMS set per Lattice's own comparison table, while the smaller LFMXO5-20TDQ/30TDQ get XMSS/LMS only.

components.name: AMD Versal Adaptive SoC
components.description: AMD Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 and Prime Series Gen 2: PQC secure boot uses Leighton-Micali Signatures (LMS, hash-based, per SHA-256/SHAKE-256); ML-KEM (Kyber) and ML-DSA (Dilithium) provide runtime encryption and runtime authentication respectively, with SLH-DSA (SPHINCS+) also available for runtime authentication.

components.name: NetApp ONTAP 9.16
components.description: Beginning with ONTAP 9.18.1, SSL in ONTAP supports the ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) post-quantum cryptographic algorithms for data-in-transit; these are negotiated only when FIPS is disabled and the peer also supports them. NetApp also markets quantum-ready data-at-rest encryption (cryptographic agility, AES-256).

components.name: Pure Storage Purity//FA 6.6
components.version: FA-1.5 (Module version); Purity OS 6.4 (Tested OS version); Platform context: Purity//FA 6.6
components.description: The document contains no mention of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), quantum-resistant algorithms, or migration plans. It exclusively details FIPS 140-3 Level 1 validation using classical cryptography (AES-256).

components.name: HPE Alletra MP
components.description: The document mentions "Quantum Security" under the Technology Leadership section but provides no specific details regarding Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) implementation, algorithms, or maturity levels for HPE Alletra Storage MP.

components.name: Commvault Cloud
components.description: Commvault Cloud (CPR 2024 / 11.36 and later) supports quantum-resistant algorithms CRYSTALS-Kyber, CRYSTALS-Dilithium, SPHINCS+ and FALCON (since Aug 2024), and added NIST's HQC algorithm in June 2025, within a cryptographic-agility framework enabled via simple configuration to defend against harvest-now-decrypt-later threats.

components.name: QuintessenceLabs qSOC
components.description: The Trusted Security Foundation (TSF) provides PQC crypto-agile key management supporting the latest NIST Quantum Resistant Algorithms. The qConnect Quantum Safe Key Distributor enables quantum safe key distribution using NIST approved PQC algorithms, standard industry protocols, and supports hybrid QKD/PQC key delivery. Integration with PQShield quantum resistant algorithm implementations is described for TSF KMS and qClient SDK.

components.name: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
components.description: AWS: Post-Quantum TLS Support in AWS KMS and Certificate Manager

components.name: Microsoft Azure
components.description: Microsoft's Quantum Safe Program now targets full transition of products and services to post-quantum cryptography by 2029 (accelerated from a prior 2033 target; announced 2026-06-30). Note this is Windows/SymCrypt-platform capability, not an Azure-service-specific claim: ML-KEM and ML-DSA are available via CNG and Certificate functions for Windows Insiders and Linux, and TLS 1.3 hybrid key exchange is enabled in SymCrypt-OpenSSL v1.9.0. As an Azure cloud service specifically, Azure Key Vault Premium (public preview) and Managed HSM support quantum-resistant AES-256 symmetric key wrapping (AES-KW/AES-GCM/AES-CBC via oct-HSM keys) per CNSA 2.0 guidance; ML-KEM/ML-DSA asymmetric PQC support is not yet documented for Azure Key Vault as of the live Microsoft Learn documentation (updated 2026-07-30).

components.name: Docker Engine 28.0
components.description: Docker Engine: built in Go. Go 1.24+ enables PQC X25519MLKEM768 by default.

components.name: Amazon EKS
components.version: AWS SDK for Java v2.0; AWS-LC-FIPS-3.0
components.description: PQC support for Amazon EKS is documented through two distinct, EKS-connected mechanisms — neither of which is AWS Transfer Family or the AWS SDK for Java v2 (both are unrelated services/libraries with no documented EKS-specific connection). (1) ALB/NLB listeners provisioned for EKS Ingress/Service resources via the AWS Load Balancer Controller can use ML-KEM hybrid post-quantum TLS security policies (e.g. ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-Res-PQ-2025-09; algorithms SecP256r1MLKEM768/SecP384r1MLKEM1024/X25519MLKEM768) — the same ML-KEM-hybrid-only capability already verified on the standalone ALB catalog row. This requires the cluster operator to explicitly select a PQ-TLS policy; AWS Load Balancer Controller-provisioned listeners do not default to one. (2) The AWS Secrets Store CSI Driver add-on for EKS (v2.0.0 or later) automatically prefers ML-KEM hybrid post-quantum TLS when pods retrieve secrets from AWS Secrets Manager, per the AWS Security Blog (published 24 Apr 2026, updated 12 Jun 2026). Not stated as a native/automatic feature of the EKS control plane itself.

components.name: Google GKE
components.description: GKE is a managed implementation of open-source Kubernetes and inherits the same TLS behavior verified for upstream Kubernetes: since Kubernetes v1.33 (April 2025), the API server and kubelet — built with Go 1.24+ — get Go crypto/tls's default hybrid post-quantum key exchange (X25519MLKEM768, combining ML-KEM-768 with classical X25519) automatically, with no GKE-specific configuration required. This covers key exchange only; GKE does not implement or use ML-DSA (FIPS 204) or SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) digital signatures. As of 2026-08-17, GKE currently supports Kubernetes minor versions 1.30-1.36 across its release channels, with per-channel defaults: Rapid 1.36.2-gke.2064000, Regular 1.35.6-gke.1641000, Stable 1.35.6-gke.1250000 — all well past v1.33, so the hybrid ML-KEM default applies across every currently supported GKE version and channel.

components.name: Azure AKS
components.description: Azure AKS: managed Kubernetes. K8s v1.33 (Go 1.24) has PQC. AKS inherits when upgrading.

components.name: Fastly Edge Cloud
components.description: Fastly ML-KEM support rollout April 2025. Globally deploying PQC hybrid TLS.

components.name: Amazon CloudFront
components.version: TLS1.3_2025 policy; AWS SDK for Java v2
components.description: Supports hybrid post-quantum key establishment across all existing TLS security policies and a new TLS 1.3 only policy (TLS1.3_2025). PQC is automatically enabled for client-to-edge connections with no customer configuration required. Available in all edge locations at no additional charge.

components.name: Google Cloud CDN
components.description: Cloud CDN has no independent TLS stack: per Google's Cloud CDN docs, it 'works with the global external Application Load Balancer or the classic Application Load Balancer to deliver content' — that Load Balancer handles TLS termination. The Load Balancer layer now documents post-quantum hybrid key exchange (X25519MLKEM768/ML-KEM): opt-in today (disabled by default), default-enabled after October 2026, always-enabled after October 2027. Cloud KMS's ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA reached General Availability (announced 2026-07-28) — no longer 'preview' — but Cloud KMS is a separate key-management product, not Cloud CDN, and is not evidence for CDN's own PQC posture. Google's company-wide PQC roadmap (published 2026-08-11) marks Load Balancers and Cloud KMS algorithms 'Completed' in 2026, with full PQC readiness convergence now targeted for 2029, not 'end of 2026.'

components.name: Zoom Post-Quantum End-to-End Encryption (Zoom Meetings, part of Zoom Workplace)
components.description: Zoom deployed post-quantum end-to-end encryption (PQ E2EE) for Zoom Meetings in May 2024, using Kyber 768 (standardized by NIST as ML-KEM in FIPS 203). As of the current support article, PQ E2EE also covers participants joining via Zoom Rooms (6.1.0+) or Zoom desktop/mobile (6.0.10+); Zoom Phone PQ E2EE support is not confirmed as live in current documentation.

components.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
components.description: Microsoft's Quantum Safe Program now targets full transition of products and services to post-quantum cryptography by 2029 (accelerated from a prior 2033 target; announced 2026-06-30). Note this is Windows/SymCrypt-platform capability, not a Defender-for-Endpoint-specific claim: ML-KEM and ML-DSA are available via CNG for Windows Insiders and Linux, and TLS 1.3 hybrid key exchange is enabled in SymCrypt-OpenSSL v1.9.0 -- Defender for Endpoint does not itself implement any of these. As a Defender for Endpoint / Defender Vulnerability Management capability specifically, the product offers a Certificate inventory feature (collected via MDE agents) that flags certificates with weak signature algorithms (e.g. SHA-1, MD5) or short RSA key sizes (<2048 bits); per the live Microsoft Learn documentation (updated 2026-06-18), this is classical cryptographic hygiene detection and includes no post-quantum-specific algorithm detection or quantum-vulnerability scoring.

components.name: Windscribe
components.description: Windscribe apps support post-quantum WireGuard out of the box using TLS 1.3 with the hybrid key exchange mechanism X25519MLKEM768 to share the PresharedKey. The PSK is rotated on each login. Validated with Wireshark.

components.name: NordVPN
components.description: NordVPN has rolled out post-quantum encryption (PQE) across all its VPN apps (Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, Android TV, tvOS, Linux). The upgrade integrates quantum-resistant algorithms into the NordLynx protocol (based on WireGuard), complying with NIST standards. Initially deployed on Linux in September 2024 to collect performance data, it expanded to all platforms in 2025. PQE is enabled via a toggle switch in settings and activates automatically when connecting via NordLynx.

components.name: Surfshark
components.description: Surfshark VPN adds post-quantum protection to its WireGuard protocol via a hybrid two-step handshake: classical Curve25519 key exchange combined with post-quantum ML-KEM (lattice-based) key encapsulation, deriving the final session key from both secrets. Enabled automatically when WireGuard is selected in the Surfshark app; not supported on manual/config-file WireGuard setups. Shipped (not roadmap) starting January 2026, first on Mac, Linux, and Android apps, with iOS and Windows support planned to follow.

components.name: Brave Browser
components.description: As a Chromium-based browser, Brave inherits X25519MLKEM768 hybrid post-quantum key agreement as the default TLS key exchange from upstream Chromium/BoringSSL, effective from Brave 1.73.x (which upgraded to Chromium 131, released November 2024). This is purely inherited, unannounced behavior: Brave's own release notes and its official CHANGELOG_DESKTOP.md contain no mention of Kyber, ML-KEM, or post-quantum cryptography, and no Brave-specific code/patches for it exist in the brave-core source tree. Brave has published no dedicated documentation or announcement of this capability.

components.name: Tor Browser
components.version: 15.0.19 (Tor Browser stable release, 2026-07-21; 16.0a9 alpha also available)
components.description: Tor Proposal 355 ('Options for postquantum circuit extension handshakes', status: Informational; author Nick Mathewson; created 2025-03-06) surveys several candidate hybrid ML-KEM/X25519 circuit-extension handshake designs and compares them for security and cost, explicitly stating 'We won't develop any of these handshakes fully here; this proposal is about exploring our alternatives.' It is a design-exploration document, not an implementation spec, and no production PQC handshake exists in Tor yet. Per a Tor Project forum thread dated 2026-08-13, cell fragmentation (Proposal 340) remains an unimplemented prerequisite that must ship before any post-quantum handshake (which exceeds current fixed Tor cell size limits) can be deployed.

components.name: MinIO Enterprise
components.version: RELEASE.2026-08-07T18-34-35Z (latest MinIO AIStor Enterprise release, confirmed via dl.min.io/aistor release-notes directory; AIStor now has its own separate release/support cadence. The open-source minio/minio GitHub repo was archived/read-only by its owner on 2026-04-25 — confirmed directly via GitHub's archive banner — and is no longer the live product; its last tag, RELEASE.2025-10-15T17-29-55Z, is stale/inapplicable to the current Enterprise product)
components.description: MinIO AIStor Enterprise: S3-compatible object storage (also Iceberg tables, SFTP files) for AI/data workloads. Built in Go. X25519MLKEM768 hybrid PQC TLS was added via an explicit merged commit (PR #21435, 'Add support for X25519MLKEM768,' merged 2025-07-19, motivated by Go 1.24's new stdlib support), shipped in minio/minio RELEASE.2025-07-23T15-54-02Z — a deliberate opt-in code change by MinIO's own team, not passive default behavior from the Go upgrade alone.

components.name: Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
components.description: Google Cloud's company-wide PQC roadmap (published 2026-08-11) targets full quantum-safe readiness by 2029 across three domains: Store-Now-Decrypt-Later mitigation (target end-2027), integrity/non-repudiation (target end-2028), and key-management foundations (target end-2028). As of Aug 2026: Application/Proxy Load Balancers and *.googleapis.com endpoints use hybrid ML-KEM (X25519MLKEM768) TLS 1.3 key exchange (completed 2026); Google's internal ALTS protocol has been quantum-confidential (KEM) since 2025, with quantum-authentic (signature) ALTS still planned for 2026/2027; and Cloud KMS reached General Availability for ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA in 2025. Certificate Authority Service (Private CA), Cloud IAM, and Cloud HSM remain on the roadmap for 2027-2028 and are not yet quantum-safe.

components.name: Futurex Cloud
components.version: CryptoHub 7.2.0.x (underlying platform version; 'Futurex Cloud' branding not found anywhere on futurex.com — see correction_notes)
components.description: Cloud-hosted encryption backed by CryptoHub HSMs with PCI HSM validated PQC. Supports ML-DSA and ML-KEM. KMES Series 3 VirtuCrypt cloud HSM.

components.name: Sectigo Certificate Manager
components.description: Sectigo Certificate Manager offers 'Private PQC': organizations can evaluate private, experimental post-quantum SSL/TLS certificates using ML-DSA (ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, ML-DSA-87) inside standard SCM policy-based approval, auditing, renewal, and revocation workflows. Hosted by Sectigo, backed by a virtual HSM; existing Sectigo Private CA customers can request access directly through SCM or via their Sectigo representative. Positioned for testing/evaluation, not public-trust certificate issuance.

components.name: Bouncy Castle C\# / Java

algorithmProperties.parameterSetIdentifier: ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, Falcon, FrodoKEM, Classic-McEliece

components.description: Official, NIST-standardized PQC support (ML-KEM/FIPS 203, ML-DSA/FIPS 204, SLH-DSA/FIPS 205) has shipped in Bouncy Castle's mainline JCA/JCE provider (Java) and BouncyCastle.Cryptography (C#/.NET) since Java 1.79 / C# 2.5.0 (Dec 2024), replacing the earlier pre-standardization Kyber/Dilithium implementations — this is mainline official library functionality, not a third-party demo/concept-study app built on an old version. Java and C# are separately versioned, independently maintained codebases (bc-java vs bc-csharp) with their own release cadence. Subsequent releases (Java 1.81/C# 2.6.1, Jun 2025, through current Java 1.85.2/LTS 2.73.12/C# 2.7.0, Aug 2026) added standardized PKCS#8 key encodings interoperable with OpenSSL 3.5+, ML-KEM TLS 1.3 cipher suites (KEM-only and hybrid) in JSSE/(D)TLS, ML-DSA/SLH-DSA support in CMS SignedData, and Java keytool compatibility. Both editions' own package descriptions also list additional NIST PQC Standardization Process candidate algorithms — Falcon, Classic McEliece, FrodoKEM, NTRU, NTRU Prime, Picnic, SABER, and BIKE — explicitly labeled 'EXPERIMENTAL and subject to change or removal' by Bouncy Castle itself, a designation distinct from the finalized ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA. SIKE and Rainbow are not offered, consistent with their removal from the NIST PQC process.

components.name: Akamai Connected Cloud
components.description: Akamai's PQC to Origin behavior for Ghost-to-Origin (G2O) connections, using TLS 1.3 hybrid key exchange with X25519MLKEM768, has progressed past the originally planned Oct 31, 2025 GA date and is now GA/stable. Current Property Manager reference documentation (dateModified 2026-08-13) states the pqcOrigin behavior v1.2's rule-format status is 'GA, stable'; the live guide page no longer contains the June 2025 Limited-Availability/contact-account-team language — it is now disabled-by-default, opt-in per property for both Standard and Enhanced TLS hostnames.

components.name: Juniper SRX Series Firewalls
components.description: Juniper SRX Series firewalls run Junos OS and provide enterprise-grade IPsec VPN, IPS, and application security. Junos OS 25.4R1 (and Junos OS Evolved 25.4R1) introduced PQC ML-DSA-87 image signatures (off-box validation only) for SRX Series and other platforms, algorithms aligned with CNSA 2.0. Separately, Junos OS has supported quantum-safe IPsec/IKEv2 via Post-Quantum Preshared Keys (PPK, RFC 8784) on SRX Series since Junos OS 22.4R1 — a symmetric pre-shared-key mixing method, not an ML-KEM-based exchange. True ML-KEM hybrid key exchange for IKEv2/IPsec (an in-band asymmetric KEM) has not shipped in Junos OS as of Release 26.2R1, the current GA release; it remains unreleased. Juniper participates in ETSI QKD and NIST PQC standards efforts.

components.name: Utimaco SecurityServer
components.description: Full PQC support via Quantum Protect application package (in-field firmware upgrade for the u.trust General Purpose HSM Se-Series; supersedes the older Q-safe extension). Supports ML-KEM, ML-DSA, LMS, HSS, XMSS, and XMSS-MT (NIST-standardized algorithms; SLH-DSA support listed as in progress by Utimaco). Highest physical security at FIPS 140-2 Level 4. Supports custom PQC algorithm loading through CryptoServer SDK. Available in network and PCIe form factors.

components.name: Ascertia ADSS PKI Server
components.description: Supports ML-KEM (FIPS 203/Kyber), ML-DSA (FIPS 204/Dilithium), SLH-DSA (FIPS 205/SPHINCS+), and Classic McEliece. Offers a PQC Starter Kit and POC for enterprise migration.

components.name: Codegic Khatim PKI Server
components.description: Khatim PKI Server v5.0 (last confirmed version) offered experimental, pre-FIPS support for PQC via Dilithium (levels 2, 3, and 5) for CA certificates, CRLs, OCSP responses, Timestamp responses, End Entity certificates, and PKCS#1 signatures; Windows OS could not verify these PQC certificates; PAdES/XAdES/CAdES/JAdES/ASiC support was planned. UPDATE (verified live 2026-08-17 via Codegic's own homepage, post dated 2026-06-23): 'Khatim PKI Server now supports production-grade PQC ML-DSA with HSM integration, conforming to FIPS 204 & PKCS#11 v3.2' — i.e. the product has moved from pre-standard experimental Dilithium to standardized ML-DSA with HSM-backed keys. Granular details (Windows-verification limitation, exact per-artifact PQC coverage, current version number) could NOT be re-confirmed on this pass: as of 2026-08-17 every dedicated Khatim PKI Server/PQC page on codegic.com, including this row's authoritative_source, returns HTTP 404 (site-wide CMS routing issue; the bare homepage and static PDF assets still serve fine, ruling out a bot-block or full outage). Recommend re-checking once page routing is restored.

components.name: CZERTAINLY
components.description: Not stated in the provided text. No mention of Post-Quantum Cryptography algorithms, migration plans, or research status.

components.name: EVERTRUST STREAM
components.description: Supports NIST-approved post-quantum algorithms including ML-DSA, ML-KEM, and SLH-DSA. The platform is described as "Crypto-Agile," allowing the issuance of post-quantum certificates now and transparent migration of existing certificates when Q-day arrives without infrastructure reconstruction.

components.name: EVERTRUST HORIZON
components.description: EverTrust Horizon is EverTrust SAS's certificate lifecycle management (CLM) / PKI automation platform, which discovers, issues, renews, revokes, and deploys digital certificates (TLS/SSL, IoT, mobile, code-signing, DevOps/CI-CD) across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid infrastructure from a single console. In September 2025, EverTrust announced that Horizon is natively compatible with Thales' Luna HSM firmware v7.9 — the first Luna HSM firmware release to support the NIST-standardized post-quantum algorithms ML-KEM (FIPS 203, key encapsulation) and ML-DSA (FIPS 204, digital signatures) in production. This lets organizations issue and hardware-protect hybrid classical/post-quantum certificates and keys through Horizon while using Luna HSMs for sovereign, HSM-backed PQC key generation and storage.

components.name: Eviden IDnomic PKI
components.description: IDnomic PKI is not yet confirmed PQC-ready. The vendor's own FAQ (cryptovision.com, CMS-modified as recently as 2026-01-20) still phrases its PQC-readiness target in future tense -- 'will be PQC-ready by End of 2023' -- rather than as a completed milestone. IDnomic PKI supports hybrid certificates allowing coexistence of classical asymmetric cryptography with PQC algorithms once selected; no specific PQC algorithm is named as implemented.

components.name: MTG AG CARA
components.description: MTG CARA is MTG AG's Certification Authority (CA) platform, the CA component of MTG Corporate PKI (alongside MTG CLM). CARA's own release notes confirm specific PQC algorithm support added incrementally: Composite ML-DSA for software keys / hybrid certificates (v3.1.0, 2026-03-23, marked EXPERIMENTAL), ML-DSA for GenericHSM-backed keys (v3.3.0, 2026-06-01), SLH-DSA for GenericHSM-backed keys (v3.4.0, 2026-06-30), and ML-KEM for software keys, end-entity certificates only (v3.5.0, 2026-07-31). CARA also enforces key-usage bit validation for ML-DSA/Composite ML-DSA/SLH-DSA keys per RFC 9881 and RFC 9909. It is designed to meet security standards such as BSI TR-03145.

components.name: MTG AG CLM
components.description: Supports MLDSA and SLHDSA algorithms. Both are explicitly labeled as "PQC, experimental" in the Supported Cryptographic Algorithms section. No production status is stated.

components.name: MTG AG KMS
components.description: Supports Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) specifically SLH-DSA and ML-DSA algorithms and their pre-hash variants. Algorithms are usable for CreateKeyPair, ReKeyKeyPair, Register, Locate, Get, Sign, and SignatureVerify operations. Implementation aligns with Draft of KMIP 3.0.

components.name: Nexus Group Certificate Manager
components.description: Certificate Manager 8.13 supports ML-KEM (FIPS 203) for end-user certificates issued via RA, CM SDK and CM REST API with client-side keys, and SLH-DSA per draft-ietf-lamps-x509-slhdsa-08.

components.name: XiPKI
components.description: Native support for post-quantum algorithms including ML-DSA (Dilithium: 44, 65, 87), ML-KEM (Kyber: 512, 768, 1024), and composite variants (MLDSA/MLKEM) per draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-sigs/kem. Supports X.509 certificates with these algorithms.

components.name: Eviden Trustway Proteccio NetHSM
components.description: The product is described as "PQC ready" and aligned with NIST recommendations to protect against "store now, decrypt later" threats. It supports specific post-quantum algorithms: ML-DSA (Signature), SLH-DSA (Signature), and ML-KEM (Key exchange). A virtual HSMaaS version is available for testing PQC live.

components.name: I4P Trident HSM
components.description: I4P's own official Trident HSM product page's Cryptography specification table lists exactly one entry under 'Post-Quantum algorithms': SPHINCS+ (= SLH-DSA) -- confirming SLH-DSA support. The same table has no ML-KEM/Kyber or ML-DSA/Dilithium entry; those algorithms named in pqc_support are not independently confirmed by this primary source. (Common Criteria certification status is out of this skill's scope.)

properties.name: pqctoday:fips_validated
properties.value: No (CC EAL4+ renewed; FIPS 140-3 on IUT list since 2025-10-14)

components.name: Utimaco uTrust HSM
components.description: Quantum Protect firmware on u.trust GP HSM Se-Series supports CAVP-validated ML-KEM, ML-DSA, LMS, HSS, and XMSS/XMSS-MT (plus SHA/SHAKE); SLH-DSA is listed by Utimaco as in progress / on the roadmap, not yet generally available. Free simulator available. NIST CAVP validation numbers 40010 and 40011, corroborated by CAVP cert #20182 for the LMS stateful hash-based signature module (folded in from the now-deprecated utimaco-quantum-protect-stateful-hash-based-signature-module row, which described the same u.trust Anchor platform). Supports custom PQC algorithm loading through CryptoServer SDK. Available in network and PCIe form factors (folded in from the now-deprecated utimaco-securityserver row, which described the same hardware line).

components.name: BERTEN MLDS-B235
components.description: Implements NIST Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard (ML-DSA) derived from CRYSTALS-Dilithium. Supports security levels 2, 3, and 5 (ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, ML-DSA-87). Includes sequencer, Polynomial Arithmetic Unit, and SHAKE XOF. Features countermeasures against Side-Channel Attacks (SCA), timing, and Simple Power Analysis (SPA). Supports Hedged variant for signing.

components.name: BERTEN MLKE-B135
components.description: BERTEN MLKE-B135 is a FIPS 203-compliant ML-KEM (Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism, derived from CRYSTALS-Kyber) IP core for FPGA, SoC, and ASIC implementation, portable to AMD (Xilinx), Intel (Altera), and Microchip (Microsemi) device families. It supports all three NIST ML-KEM parameter sets: ML-KEM-512 (Security Category 1), ML-KEM-768 (Category 3), and ML-KEM-1024 (Category 5). The core integrates a dedicated sequencer, a Polynomial Arithmetic Unit, and high-performance SHA-3/SHAKE functions, exposing four AXI4-Stream data interfaces plus one AXI4-Lite register-map interface (user-programmable to select ML-KEM operation and parameter set) and a status-notification port. At 300 MHz the vendor reports throughput of up to 87,050 key-generation, 70,500 encapsulation, and 52,300 decapsulation operations/second at ML-KEM-512, scaling to 36,500/32,200/25,600 ops/s at ML-KEM-1024, with resource usage of roughly 8.6K-17.4K LUTs and 7.4K-8.0K registers depending on target device. Countermeasures include resistance to timing and Simple Power Analysis (SPA) side-channel attacks, FIPS 203 input validation, and automatic/on-demand zeroization of internal memories and registers. Deliverables under a perpetual site license (12 months support) include an encrypted netlist, design constraints, simulation model, user manual, and ANSI C drivers.

components.name: CAST KiviPQC-KEM
components.description: Implements Module Lattice-based Key Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM) per NIST FIPS 203. Supports all three parameter sets: ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768, and ML-KEM-1024. Offers key generation, encapsulation, and decapsulation procedures. Available in Fast (F) and Tiny (T) versions for ASIC/FPGA integration. Includes protection against timing-based side channel attacks.

components.name: IP Cores PQC1
components.version: 1.1 (dated 2025-05-20, initial release, per IP Cores, Inc. PQC1 datasheet revision history)
components.description: Implements ML-KEM (FIPS-203, Kyber) and ML-DSA (FIPS-204, Dilithium) algorithms. Supports all FIPS-204 categories (ML-DSA-44, 65, 87) and FIPS-203 levels (ML-KEM-512, 768, 1024). Includes built-in NTT and SHAKE128/SHAKE256/SHA-3 engines. Contains three accelerators: NTT, FIPS-202 (SHA-3/SHAKE), and packing/unpacking. True random number generator is not included but TRNG1 core can be used.

components.name: Resquant Crypto Accelerator
components.description: Hardware PQC accelerator IP core supporting ML-KEM (Kyber), ML-DSA (Dilithium), SLH-DSA (SPHINCS+), XMSS, SHAKE, and AES as FPGA/ASIC IP cores.

components.name: Secure-IC Securyzr
components.version: V4.0 (product-sheet revision stated on both the SCZ_IP_PQC_Lattice and SCZ_IP_PQC_XMSS current product sheets; no separate IP-core version number is published)
components.description: Securyzr Tunable Cryptography PQC IP portfolio: SCZ_IP_PQC_Lattice is a hybrid hardware/software accelerator (VHDL RTL, AMBA AXI interface) supporting ML-KEM-512/768/1024 and ML-DSA-II/III/V (NIST security categories 2/3/5), with side-channel protection (SPA/DPA/DEMA/CPA/CEMA). SCZ_IP_PQC_XMSS is a software IP (per RFC 8391) implementing XMSS-SHA2_10_256 and XMSS-SHA2_16_256, running on the host CPU using a SHA-2 hash core (hardware or software). Part of Secure-IC's Securyzr embedded security IP platform.

components.name: CryptoNext Quantum-Safe Library
components.description: Secure post-quantum cryptographic library in C/C++/Assembly with multi-language wrappers (Go, Rust, Python, Java). Supports ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, plus stateful hash-based signature schemes LMS, HSS, XMSS, and XMSS-MT, and additionally Falcon and FrodoKEM. Offered in Standard, Embedded, and Side-Channel Attack Resistant editions. No evidence of X.509 Catalyst/Chimera composite certificate support was found on CryptoNext's own site; the PKI Consortium's PQC Capabilities Matrix explicitly marks Catalyst/Chimera as unsupported for this product.

components.name: Dell BSAFE Crypto Module for C
components.description: Post-quantum algorithm support is delivered via the separate Dell BSAFE Crypto Module Quantum-Resistant (QR) Plugin add-on, not the base module alone: full ML-DSA support (key generation, signing, and verification, per FIPS 204) and LMS signature VERIFICATION ONLY (per NIST SP 800-208) — the plugin does not generate LMS keys or create LMS signatures. ML-KEM support remains unconfirmed in vendor documentation found.

components.name: Dell BSAFE Crypto-J
components.description: Java-based cryptographic module. Supports ML-DSA (FIPS 204) and HSS/LMS signature verification (RFC 8554 §6.3), added in Crypto-J 7.1 (GA July 30, 2025). ML-KEM support planned (not independently confirmed in vendor documentation found).

components.name: DigiCert TrustCore SDK
components.description: ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA. TLS 1.3 hybrid X25519MLKEM768. Open-source Aug 2025.

components.name: PQ Code Package
components.version: mlkem-native v2.0.0 (released 2026-08-07); mldsa-native v2.0.0 (released 2026-08-07, first stable release)
components.description: The project (a Linux Foundation Post-Quantum Cryptography Alliance project) builds high-assurance implementations of standards-track PQC algorithms: ML-KEM (FIPS 203) via mlkem-native and ML-DSA (FIPS 204) via mldsa-native, both C90 with formally-verified (CBMC for C memory/type safety; HOL-Light for assembly functional correctness and constant-time behavior) AArch64 and x86_64 assembly backends. A separate Rust ML-KEM implementation (rust-libcrux, derived from libcrux) is formally verified for panic freedom, correctness, and secret independence using F*/hax; it does not yet cover ML-DSA. mlkem-native also includes an experimental, disabled-by-default backend for 32-bit Armv8.1-M (Helium) microcontrollers; the project's earlier dedicated embedded repo (mlkem-c-embedded) was archived in December 2025 in favor of this. A work-in-progress SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) implementation (slhdsa-c) also exists but its own README states it is not yet recommended for production use.

components.name: Cryptomathic CrystalKey 360
components.description: Cryptomathic's own current live pages describe CrystalKey 360 only in crypto-agility terms — centralized policy/algorithm/key governance across HSMs, cloud key stores, and applications — and name no specific PQC algorithms. The PKI Consortium's PQC Capabilities Matrix (pkic.org/wg/pqc/pqccm, GitHub-sourced row last updated 2025-08-14) is more specific: it lists CrystalKey 360 as currently supporting ML-DSA, LMS, and XMSS, with ML-KEM on the roadmap (not yet confirmed shipped) and SLH-DSA explicitly not supported.

components.name: ANKATech ANKASecure

algorithmProperties.parameterSetIdentifier: ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, Falcon, HQC, FrodoKEM

components.description: REST API/SaaS platform supporting ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, Falcon, LMS, XMSS, FrodoKEM, and HQC. NIST PQC compliant and NSA CNSA 2.0 aligned.

components.name: Ascertia ADSS Signing Server
components.description: Supports ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and ML-DSA (FIPS 204) for PQC-signed documents and hybrid schemes. SLH-DSA and full PQC timestamp support (PAdES LTA) in progress.

components.name: Ascertia ADSS Server/SAM
components.version: 8.4.1 (ADSS Server platform, released 2026-06-24; SAM's ML-DSA support was demonstrated while the platform was at 8.4, per the Apr-May 2026 blog series)
components.description: ADSS SAM (Signature Activation Module — Ascertia's own term, not 'Signing and Authentication Module') is the ADSS Server module/appliance that provides remote qualified-signature authorization. Ascertia's 2026 PQC blog series confirms ML-DSA (FIPS 204) support for ADSS SAM Appliance server-side PKCS#1 signatures, part of platform-wide PQC support first introduced in ADSS Server 8.3.5 (Jul 2024) and refined through 8.4 (RFC 9881/9882 conformance). ML-KEM (FIPS 203) is confirmed for ADSS Server's PKI/certificate services generally but is not specifically documented for the SAM module itself. SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) remains unconfirmed as shipped.

components.name: Codegic Khatim Sign Server
components.description: Khatim PKI Server v5.0 offers experimental support for PQC, specifically the Dilithium algorithm (levels 2, 3, and 5). It supports generating CA certificates, CRLs, OCSP responses, timestamp responses, end-entity certificates, and PKCS#1 signatures using Dilithium. Note: Windows OS currently does not support verifying these PQC certificates. Future support for PAdES, XAdES, CAdES, JAdES, and ASic is planned (experimental Dilithium pre-FIPS; not FIPS 204/ML-DSA compliant)

components.name: DigiCert Device Trust Manager
components.description: Supports ML-DSA pure PQC certificate issuance and composite ML-DSA+classical hybrid over EST, SCEP, ACME, CMPv2, REST API. ML-KEM and SLH-DSA not yet confirmed in Device Trust Manager docs.

components.name: ExeQuantum
components.description: PQC-as-a-Service platform (CipherForge) built around ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA, with hardened and formally verified implementations. Supports on-premise, air-gapped, hybrid, and cloud deployments.

components.name: essendi xc
components.description: essendi xc 3.1 (released March 19, 2026) adds integrated support for post-quantum cryptography, enabling PQC certificates to be requested and issued. essendi's current public documentation does not name specific PQC algorithms — its published supported-algorithm list still states RSA, DSA, ECC — so ML-DSA/SLH-DSA support cannot be independently confirmed from vendor sources at this time. Also adds an installation wizard, event-driven rule-based automation, and bulk certificate request. Retains discovery, lifecycle management and quantum-readiness/crypto-agility focus.

components.name: noble-post-quantum
components.description: Pure JavaScript/TypeScript implementation of ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), SLH-DSA (FIPS 205), and Falcon (added v0.6.0, prepping for FN-DSA/FIPS 206), plus hybrid KEMs: ml_kem768_x25519 (implements X-Wing directly; the legacy 'XWing' export alias was removed in v0.7.0), ml_kem768_p256, ml_kem1024_p384, plus KitchenSink and QSF/C2PRI variants. Minimal (not zero) dependencies: 3 same-author @noble packages (noble-hashes, noble-curves, noble-ciphers). Self-audited only (not yet independently audited per README). Works in browser and Node.js. Maintained by individual developer Paul Miller as part of the @noble family — no corporate affiliation found.

components.name: SUPERCOP
components.description: System for Unified Performance Evaluation Related to Cryptographic Operations and Primitives. Provides standardised benchmarking for all NIST PQC candidates and standardised algorithms including ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, HQC, and Classic McEliece. Reference benchmarks used by algorithm designers and NIST evaluators.

components.name: American Binary Ambit Client
components.description: Enterprise VPN using exclusively CNSA 2.0 PQC algorithms with MaxKyber protocol. Available on Oracle Cloud Marketplace.

components.name: Alibaba Cloud GVSM
components.description: Beta 'GVSM PQC version' (General Virtual Security Module), a China-mainland-only cipher-machine offering within Alibaba Cloud's Cloud HSM/KMS service. components.name: Caddy Server

components.name: AdGuard DNS

Enabled by default in the AdGuard DNS service since v2.19, but only usable through AdGuard's own client apps (initially Nightly/beta builds for Windows, Android, and Mac) — most operating systems and generic DoT/DoH/DoQ clients do not support it natively, and AdGuard VPN app support was not yet available at launch.

components.name: Broadcom Emulex SecureHBA

components.name: Dashlane

components.name: Utimaco Quantum Protect Suite

components.name: Oracle Linux 9.7

components.description: Quantum-safe security with cipher translation proxy, quantum readiness dashboard. 14 new NGFW models.

A third-party KubeCon NA 2025 conference demo ("Beyond Classical Cryptography: Building Quantum-Resistant Cloud-Native Infrastructure with SPIFFE") showed SPIRE issuing ML-DSA (Dilithium3) X.509 certificates with Cilium/Envoy enforcing ML-KEM (Kyber) key exchange for mTLS — this is a conference proof-of-concept documented only in a third-party blog (gluo.be), absent from both the official Cilium 1.19 and 1.20 release notes.

components.name: Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh PQC
components.description: OpenShift Service Mesh 3.3: quantum-secure Istio gateways and in-mesh traffic.

components.name: OVHcloud QRNG SSL
components.description: QRNG (via Quandela's MosaiQ photonic quantum computer) supplies quantum-derived entropy for classical SSL/TLS key generation across ~5 million OVHcloud-hosted websites (100% of Let's Encrypt certs by Nov 2025). This strengthens randomness quality, not the cryptographic algorithm itself - no ML-KEM/ML-DSA or other PQC algorithm is used. OVHcloud's R&D department separately states it is developing PQC (and QKD) 'following recommendations from ANSSI', per a distinct Jun 10, 2025 press release - that work is not yet integrated into this feature.

components.name: Threema PQC
components.description: Quantum-secure messaging with IBM Research partnership for ML-KEM integration.

components.name: SimpleX Chat PQC

components.name: Session Protocol V2 PQC
