components.name: Thunderbird PQC (OpenPGP)
components.description: OpenPGP PQC (RFC 9980: composite ML-KEM+ECC encryption, composite ML-DSA/standalone SLH-DSA signatures) is implemented via the RNP OpenPGP library, which uses Botan as its cryptographic backend; a large PQC pull request for RNP is in progress. Thunderbird already has experimental v4 PQC message support; full stable support is targeted by end of 2026. S/MIME PQC (also via Botan) remains at research stage, not yet deployed, pending broader standards agreement. Work originated from the BSI-funded PQC@Thunderbird project (Dec 2021-Dec 2024, led by MTG AG, with BSI and Proton AG co-developing the OpenPGP draft that became RFC 9980).

components.name: CISA PQC Migration Framework
components.description: CISA's "Product Categories for Technologies That Use Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards" (published Jan 23, 2026, pursuant to Executive Order 14306). Lists hardware/software product categories with PQC-capable products already widely available (Cloud Services, Collaboration Software, Web Software, Endpoint Security) and categories still transitioning to PQC (Networking Hardware/Software, ICAM, Storage, Data/Database, Telecom Hardware, Computers, Enterprise Security). Federal procurement guidance for FCEB agencies, not a software product.

components.name: Java 24 PQC Runtime
components.description: JEP 496 (ML-KEM, FIPS 203) and JEP 497 (ML-DSA, FIPS 204) shipped as finalized (non-preview) cryptographic primitive APIs in JDK 24 (GA 2025-03-18) — confirmed via OpenJDK's own JEP pages, both Status: Closed/Delivered, Release: 24. JEP 527 (hybrid ML-KEM+ECDHE TLS 1.3 key exchange: X25519MLKEM768, SecP256r1MLKEM768, SecP384r1MLKEM1024, default-on via javax.net.ssl) has now been integrated into the JDK 27 codebase (Status: Closed/Delivered, Release: 27, updated 2026-08-10), but JDK 27 itself has not reached General Availability — GA is scheduled for 2026-09-15. The current GA release is JDK 26 (released 2026-03-17); its official feature list does not include JEP 527, and SunJSSE/JSSE does not offer the hybrid TLS named groups by default through JDK 26.

components.name: pqcrypto Python Library
components.description: Python PQC library with KEMs and signatures. CPython 3.14 support.

components.name: Applivery UEM PQC
components.version: Not applicable — continuously deployed SaaS; no discrete version number publicly stated
components.description: First UEM to deploy PQC across managed Apple devices using Post-quantum Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) X25519MLKEM768 (ML-KEM-768 + X25519) with AES-256, via Apple quantum-secure TLS 1.3 APIs on iOS/macOS/iPadOS 26 and TLS 1.3 over OpenSSL 3.5.0 on servers.

components.name: Opera Browser PQC
components.description: Chromium-based browser with hybrid PQC key exchange enabled by default.

components.name: Internxt Drive PQC
components.description: Zero-knowledge encrypted cloud storage with post-quantum encryption. EU-based privacy focus.

components.name: Algorand FALCON Mainnet
components.version: go-algorand v5.0.0 (released Aug 12, 2026; consensus upgrade cleared 90% node support Aug 15, 2026; MainNet activation pending as of Aug 2026)
components.description: Algorand states it pioneered live Falcon-based post-quantum account signatures on the mainnet of a major/mainstream L1 blockchain (Nov 2025). FALCON has also signed Algorand's compact State Proofs since 2022. Falcon (FN-DSA) was selected by NIST for standardization, but the FIPS 206 standard itself remains in development at NIST as of Aug 2026 and has not yet been finalized/published.

components.name: Versa Networks SASE PQC
components.description: Quantum-safe SASE: hybrid PQC key exchange (ECDH/X25519 + ML-KEM512/1024) shipped and running now across SD-WAN, SSE, and ZTNA IPsec tunnels on the VersaONE Universal SASE / VOS platform, on existing appliance hardware without a forklift upgrade.

components.name: Netskope One PQC
components.description: Cloud SASE platform preparing ML-KEM (specifically ML-KEM 768) post-quantum key exchange for secure web gateway and ZTNA. Per Netskope's own blog, the quantum-resilient version of Netskope One is still in development, not yet shipped/GA.

components.name: Tailscale PQC
components.description: Zero-config mesh VPN with post-quantum hybrid key exchange. Based on WireGuard.

components.name: NGINX Plus R33 PQC
components.description: Enterprise reverse proxy/load balancer; R33 added initial Post-Quantum Cryptography support (via oqs-provider for OpenSSL 3.x). Native OpenSSL 3.5 (X25519MLKEM768 by default) support added in later releases (R36+).

components.name: Trezor Safe 7 PQC
components.description: Hardware wallet using SLH-DSA-128 (SPHINCS+) hybrid with Ed25519 for bootloader/firmware verification, and ML-DSA-44 for device attestation/certificate. Transaction/wallet signing still uses classical ECDSA/EdDSA — blockchains have not yet adopted PQC, so no PQC algorithm protects transaction signing today. Began shipping Nov 23, 2025 (international; US shipments delayed by FCC-certification backlog during the government shutdown).

components.name: QAN XLINK PQC
components.description: QAN XLINK is a quantum-resistant cross-signer ('digital security layer') that adds ML-DSA (FIPS 204 / CRYSTALS-Dilithium) post-quantum signatures to existing Ethereum-compatible wallets (e.g. MetaMask, Trust Wallet), cross-signing transactions so EVM accounts stay protected if quantum computers break ECDSA. It is a separate product from the QANplatform Layer-1 blockchain, which is what provides native multi-language smart contracts; XLINK itself does not execute smart contracts.

components.name: ZeroTier Quantum
components.description: Software-defined networking platform with hybrid FIPS-compliant PQC at the transport layer (ZTP). Combines ML-KEM-1024, ML-DSA-87, P-384 ECC. First SDN solution meeting NSA CNSA 2.0. Announced at RSAC 2026 on March 23, 2026; reached Release Candidate 2 (RC2) on June 25, 2026, described by ZeroTier as one step from general availability pending third-party code audit and penetration testing. As of the Aug 6, 2026 Carahsoft/SEWP V partnership announcement, no distinct GA release or new version had been separately confirmed.

components.name: Quantropi QiSpace STM32
components.version: Not publicly stated — QiSpace is delivered as a continuously updated SaaS/cloud platform; no version number found in Quantropi's own site, product briefs, or STMicroelectronics/Renesas partner pages as of 2026-08
components.description: Post-quantum secure boot, TLS, and application-layer cryptography for STM32 Cortex-M/MPU microcontrollers via the QiSpace PQC for IoT SDK. Baseline package uses NIST-standardized ML-KEM/ML-DSA (FIPS 203/204); Premium package adds Quantropi's proprietary HPPK-KEM/GHPPK-DS post-quantum algorithms and QEEP symmetric encryption for smaller footprint/higher performance.

components.name: IBM z17 Quantum Safe
components.description: IBM z17 mainframe with quantum-safe cryptographic acceleration. CNSA 2.0 compliant hardware crypto.

components.name: LTO-10 PQC-Ready Tape
components.description: LTO-10 tape format co-developed by the LTO Program (HPE, IBM, Quantum Corporation). Initial specifications (30 TB native / 75 TB compressed at 2.5:1) publicly released Aug 13, 2025; a 40 TB native / 100 TB compressed cartridge specification was announced separately on Nov 12, 2025. LTO-10 drives use hardware-based, quantum-safe AES/GCM-256 encryption and are post-quantum cryptography key-exchange ready per the LTO Program's own specification announcement; WORM cartridges are supported.

components.name: ASUSTOR ADM 5.1 PQC
components.description: NAS operating system with Kyber/ML-KEM TLS for management interface. SOHO/SMB quantum readiness.

components.name: IBM LinuxONE PQC
components.description: Linux mainframe with quantum-safe cryptographic coprocessor. PKCS#11 PQC API support.

components.name: Forward Edge-AI Space Router
components.version: No public version — in development under Phase II SBIR (Space Development Agency); vendor's own page labels it "Direct to Phase II SBIR," no commercial release number issued
components.description: Space-grade edge AI router with PQC-secured communications for LEO satellite constellations.

components.name: Arqit 6WIND Telco PQC
components.version: Not applicable – no distinct product version number is published for this integration (partnership/technology integration announced 2026-02-19; NetworkSecure and 6WIND VSR are each versioned separately by their vendors, but no combined version identifier exists)
components.description: Integration combining Arqit NetworkSecure quantum-safe key generation with 6WIND Virtual Service Router for on-device quantum-safe IPsec across uCPE and virtualised cloud; supports site-to-site, hub-and-spoke, and high-availability deployments. Launched Feb 19, 2026. Underlying technology: NetworkSecure's key generation uses Arqit's own proprietary Symmetric Key Agreement (SKA)/QuantumCloud platform — not NIST-standardized ML-KEM/ML-DSA key establishment. Arqit states NetworkSecure 'complies with' NIST ML-KEM and RFC 8784 (post-quantum preshared keys mixed into IKEv2) for standards conformance/interop, but the actual quantum-safe key material is generated by Arqit's proprietary SKA mechanism and injected as a preshared key, not produced via the ML-KEM algorithm itself.

components.name: Qrypt VPN for NVIDIA Jetson
components.version: No single published product version; deployment stack per vendor docs: strongSwan 6.0.0beta4 + liboqs 0.11.0 + custom Qrypt Yocto BSP (Scarthgap 5.0) on Linux kernel 6.6 LTS
components.description: Hybrid PQC IPsec VPN for NVIDIA Jetson robotics/edge AI platforms: strongSwan 6.0 + liboqs 0.11.0 provide ML-KEM-768 post-quantum key exchange, while the Qrypt BLAST plugin independently generates matching quantum-entropy-sourced (QRNG) keys at each endpoint (no key ever transmitted over the network) as a defense-in-depth layer. Live on Jetson Orin Nano/NX; Jetson Thor AGX support added.

components.name: CIQ Rocky Linux CAVP PQC
components.version: Rocky Linux from CIQ (RLC) 9.6 was the version cited in CIQ's Feb 2026 NSS 3.112 ML-KEM/ML-DSA announcement, but is stale as a 'current' version claim — CIQ's product line and upstream Rocky Linux have since progressed through RLC 9.7 (Dec 2025) and Rocky Linux 9.8 / 10.2 (May 2026); CIQ's own roadmap already references 'Rocky Linux from CIQ 10.2' for a separate OpenSSL PQC validation targeted Q3 2026.
components.description: Rocky Linux with NIST CAVP-certified PQC algorithms in NSS crypto library.

components.name: BTQ Bitcoin Quantum Testnet
components.description: Quantum-resistant fork of Bitcoin testing BIP 360 Pay-to-Merkle-Root (P2MR) outputs and NIST-standardized ML-DSA (CRYSTALS-Dilithium, FIPS 204) signatures for transaction signing, run as a live public testnet with an open-source contributor community.

components.name: QRL 2.0 (Quantum Resistant Ledger)
components.description: Purpose-built quantum-resistant blockchain. QRL 1.x mainnet has used XMSS hash-based signatures since 2018. QRL 2.0 (Project Zond), an EVM-compatible proof-of-stake successor chain, integrates ML-DSA-87 (CRYSTALS-Dilithium) as its mandatory signature scheme — this is already shipped and live on the public QRL 2.0 Testnet V2 (launched 2026-03-31), not merely planned. QRL 2.0 mainnet launch date is undetermined, pending completion of independent security audits.

components.name: NXP i.MX 94 PQC Processor
components.description: First applications processor integrating PQC via EdgeLock Secure Enclave (Advanced Profile): hybrid-mode signing (ML-DSA + classical ECDSA) of NXP-signed Secure Enclave Firmware, enabling a post-quantum hardware root-of-trust for secure boot, secure debug, and secure update. Target applications span Industrial Automation, Building Control & Energy, and Automotive — not automotive-exclusive. V2X authentication/encryption is provided by a separate block (EdgeLock Accelerator/Prime); NXP's own materials describe it only generically, with no stated PQC linkage for V2X specifically.

components.name: NXP OrangeBox 2.0 PQC
components.description: Connectivity domain controller with on-device AI and PQC for software-defined vehicles.

components.description: PQC consulting service (management-guidance workshops, technical migration analysis for PKI/key-management systems, E/E-architecture integration) plus ESCRYPT CycurHSM 3.x HSM firmware, confirmed by ETAS's own Feb 2024 press release to already enable post-quantum cryptography. No live ETAS documentation ties PQC specifically to V2X (a separate, unrelated ETAS webinar/offering with no PQC content) or to secure boot (a general HSM feature, not described as PQC-specific).

PQC Client to Edge is now enabled by default for all Enhanced TLS hostnames (Standard TLS: limited availability, disabled by default). PQC to Origin is GA/stable but opt-in for both TLS types.

components.name: Fastly PQC CDN

components.name: PQChat Quantum-Safe Messaging
components.description: Quantum-safe end-to-end encrypted messaging app using the Classic McEliece code-based cryptosystem (Post-Quantum Ltd's flagship algorithm, a NIST PQC Round 4 finalist). Now distributed enterprise-only after removal from public app stores.

components.name: Proton Mail PQC OpenPGP
components.version: Mail app v7.0.0 (Android/iOS) — minimum version documented by Proton as required to access post-quantum protection; no distinct web/desktop version number published
components.description: Post-quantum protection shipped as a live, opt-in feature in Proton Mail (gradual rollout, all plans incl. free), using RFC 9980 composite ML-KEM-768 + X25519 hybrid encryption within OpenPGP v6. Proton AG (via cryptographer Aron Wussler) co-authored RFC 9980 with BSI and MTG AG. Feature applies to new emails only (not retroactive) and is currently incompatible with end-to-end encrypted forwarding.

components.name: TrustCloud Quantum Vault
components.description: Post-quantum encryption for preserving digital agreements. DocuSign App Center integration. eIDAS/HIPAA compliant.

components.name: SignQuantum PQC E-Signature

Integrates with DocuSign, Adobe Acrobat Sign, PandaDoc, Dropbox Sign, and Signaturit Group; customizable for other providers.

components.name: Microchip MEC175xB PQC Controllers
components.description: Low-power embedded controllers with immutable hardware-based PQC. Arm Cortex-M4F, CNSA 2.0 compliant.

components.name: Rambus QSE IP
components.description: QSE-IP-86 Quantum Safe Engine IP core for ASIC, SoC, FPGA. Accelerates ML-KEM (FIPS 203, up to Cat 5, 13,500 encap/s @1GHz), ML-DSA (FIPS 204, up to Cat 5, ~1,400 sign/s @1GHz), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205); integrated SHA-3/SHAKE. NIST CAVP certified; usable in FIPS 140-3 compliant product. DPA-protected variant QSE-IP-86-DPA available.

components.name: Dyber QuantaTPM

components.name: PQSecure Technologies HW IP

components.name: NVIDIA cuPQC SDK

On NVIDIA H100 vs single-core AMD EPYC 7313P CPU: ML-DSA-65 achieves 6.5M keygen/s (290x), 5.0M verify/s (215x), 0.6M sign/s (65x); ML-KEM-768 achieves 13.5M keygen/s (175x), 9.0M encap/s (120x), 8.5M decap/s (135x). SDK also includes cuPQC-Hash (SHA-2/SHA-3/SHAKE/Poseidon2) and Merkle tree acceleration.

components.name: STMicroelectronics X-CUBE-PQC
components.description: PQC software library for STM32H563xx (Arm Cortex-M33) microcontrollers: ML-KEM key encapsulation/decapsulation, ML-DSA digital signature generation/verification, and LMS/XMSS stateful hash-based signature verification used mainly for secure boot code and firmware authentication. Product status is NRND (Not Recommended for New Design) on ST's own live product page; ST directs new designs to X-CUBE-CRYPTOLIB, whose V5.x.x release folded in these same PQC algorithms (previously delivered separately as X-CUBE-PQC).

components.name: Renesas Veridify PQC for RA MCUs
components.description: Veridify's DOME identity platform page (the catalog's own cited proof_url, veridify.com/dome/) states support for FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), and FALCON. However, that page makes no mention of Renesas or RA MCUs, and the previously archived CES press-release proof for the Renesas partnership is a dead link (404, confirmed by direct fetch). The Renesas RA MCU + Veridify PQC claim is currently unconfirmed by any live source.

components.name: Sequoia-PGP PQC
components.description: OpenPGP implementation maintained by the independent Sequoia PGP project (primarily funded by the p≡p Foundation). Hybrid PQC support (ML-DSA-87/Ed448 signing, ML-KEM-1024/X448 and ML-KEM-768/X25519 encryption) was developed in collaboration with Red Hat, which funded/contributed engineering for this feature and uses it to sign RHEL 10.1 RPM packages with ML-DSA-87/Ed448 hybrid keys as a technology preview.

components.name: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 PQC

components.version: Stable 6.5.6 (released 2026-03-25); development track 6.6.2 RC (2026-06-17), 6.6.3 in progress; ML-KEM since 6.4.2 beta (2025-01-27), NTRU Prime since 6.4 beta (2024-09-19)

ML-KEM/FIPS 203 IPSec VPN) via a Palo Alto Networks NGFW integration/MoU. Progressed from an enterprise-trial pilot (Aug 2024) to the commercial 'Hybrid QSN' launch (Oct 23, 2025).

components.name: IBM z16 Crypto Express 8S
components.description: IBM Crypto Express 8S (CEX8S) is the hardware security module integrated into IBM z16 mainframes. CEX8S operates in EP11 (IBM Enterprise PKCS#11) mode supporting quantum-safe algorithms including Kyber (ML-KEM) and Dilithium (ML-DSA) via the IBM Quantum Safe Cryptography API. Achieved FIPS 140-3 Level 4 certification (the highest level available). EP11 firmware provides quantum-safe key generation, encapsulation/decapsulation, and signing operations. Used in IBM LinuxONE and IBM Z as the hardware root of trust for quantum-safe workloads. IBM Quantum Safe Toolkit integrates with CEX8S for crypto discovery and migration.

components.name: AWS Certificate Manager
components.description: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) provisions and manages TLS/SSL certificates for AWS services. ACM-issued certificate endpoints use hybrid ML-KEM TLS key exchange (via AWS-LC FIPS 140-3 validated module) protecting certificate delivery in transit. AWS Private CA (ACM Private CA), the companion service, supports ML-DSA-44/65/87 (FIPS 204) certificate issuance for private PKI since June 2025, enabling quantum-safe code signing, mutual TLS, and device identity workflows. Public ACM certificates (issued via ACM free tier) currently use classical RSA/ECDSA; PQC public certificate issuance depends on CA/Browser Forum ballot adoption. ACM integrates with AWS KMS for private key storage with FIPS 140-3 Level 3 HSM backing.

components.name: Cosmian KMS
components.description: Full ML-KEM-512/768/1024 (FIPS 203) ML-DSA-44/65/87 (FIPS 204) and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) in production since v5.12+. KMIP 2.1 server. Hybrid KEM combiner (classical + PQC via SHA-256). Covercrypt attribute-based encryption. Only open-source KMIP server with full NIST PQC algorithm suite shipping today.

components.name: Certicom Code Signing and Key Management Server
components.description: Certicom's own Code Signing and Key Management Server product page confirms support for 'quantum resistant digital signature algorithms' alongside traditional RSA/ECDSA. Certicom's own datasheet (v9, hosted at certicom.com) independently confirms specific algorithm names directly: 'Traditional RSA, ECDSA & Quantum Resistant LMS, XMSS and Dilithium digital signatures.' This datasheet is dated approximately 2022 (pre-dates FIPS 204 finalization; still uses 'Dilithium' rather than 'ML-DSA', and does not mention ML-KEM) but is genuinely Certicom's own first-party documentation. The specific claim that it uses ML-DSA (Dilithium) with NXP S32G secure boot for automotive OTA/SBOM signing still comes only from the separate BlackBerry/NXP joint announcement (electronicspecifier.com), not from Certicom's own documentation.

components.name: BlackBerry QNX Hypervisor 8.0 for Safety
components.description: Safety-certified embedded hypervisor (ISO 26262 ASIL D, IEC 61508 SIL 4). BlackBerry has demonstrated quantum-resistant (Dilithium) code-signing and secure-boot concepts with NXP for automotive firmware/OTA, but no confirmed PQC integration into Hypervisor 8.0 specifically, and no confirmed automaker adoption of this PQC capability.

components.name: OpenSSL 3.5.0
components.description: First OpenSSL release with native ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA support without the OQS provider. X25519MLKEM768 hybrid key exchange enabled by default in TLS 1.3. Released April 29, 2025.

components.name: Utimaco Athos
components.description: Payment HSM with PQC on roadmap. Utimaco SecurityServer general-purpose HSM has announced PQC roadmap for NIST algorithms. Athos payment-specific HSM firmware does not yet publicly list ML-KEM or ML-DSA support. German vendor positioning for European PCI DSS and EMV compliance.

components.name: UEFI Forum Secure Boot
components.description: No PQC algorithm support in current UEFI Secure Boot specification (UEFI 2.10). Signature database supports RSA-2048 SHA-256 only. However, AMI achieved the industry's first working PQC implementation in Aptio V UEFI Firmware (November 2025). CNSA 2.0 mandates PQC firmware signing as the first use case starting 2025. Doug Flick (Microsoft) added as TianoCore EDK2 CryptoPkg maintainer for PQC (Feb 2026). Future revisions expected to add ML-DSA/SLH-DSA.

components.name: Windows Secure Boot
components.description: No PQC firmware signature verification in current Secure Boot. CNG supports ML-KEM/ML-DSA for applications but Secure Boot chain still uses RSA-2048.

components.name: Oracle TDE
components.description: Oracle Database 26ai introduces quantum-resistant encryption for Transparent Data Encryption. Includes support for post-quantum cryptographic algorithms for data-at-rest protection. Key management via Oracle Key Vault (OKV) with classical key wrapping pending PQC upgrade. Significant milestone as first major RDBMS to ship PQC-capable TDE. Note: ML-KEM/ML-DSA are for TLS in-transit encryption (Oracle 26ai). TDE data-at-rest uses AES-256 (quantum-resistant symmetric).

Google has not announced a specific ML-DSA migration timeline for identity tokens.

components.name: AnyDesk

Transport upgrade to ML-KEM hybrid TLS expected to follow BSI TR-02102 updates.

components.name: Robust Intelligence AI Firewall

components.name: Thales CipherTrust Data Discovery and Classification

components.name: Entrust KeyControl
components.description: Full PQC key management with ML-KEM ML-DSA and SLH-DSA key types. Supports encapsulation decapsulation sign and verify operations. PQ-TLS for KMIP connections. nShield 5 HSM v13.8.0 natively supports PQC with CAVP validation.

components.name: Windows Server 2025
components.description: General availability of PQC algorithms in November 2025 update. Supports ML-KEM and ML-DSA via CNG and Certificate functions.

components.name: OQS-OpenSSL Provider (liboqs-provider)

algorithmProperties.parameterSetIdentifier: ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, Falcon, HQC, Classic-McEliece

components.description: The OQS OpenSSL provider (liboqs-provider) is the canonical bridge from liboqs to OpenSSL 3.x. It provides all NIST-standardized PQC algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, FN-DSA) plus round 4 candidates (HQC, BIKE, Classic McEliece) as an OpenSSL provider plugin. Enables PQC TLS 1.3, PQC X.509 certificates, and PQC key operations in any application using OpenSSL 3.x without code changes. Maintained by the Open Quantum Safe project.

components.name: libcrux
components.description: Formally verified Rust implementation of ML-KEM and ML-DSA by Cryspen. Code extracted from HACL* and verified using the hax toolchain for panic-freedom and functional correctness. Supports all parameter sets for both algorithms. Used in production by Firefox and other projects.

components.name: Trail of Bits ml-dsa
components.description: Constant-time pure Go implementation of ML-DSA (FIPS 204) by Trail of Bits. Supports ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, and ML-DSA-87. Designed for side-channel resistance using Barrett reduction and branchless operations to avoid KyberSlash-style timing leaks.

components.name: Venafi
components.description: Venafi TLS Protect and CodeSign Protect support experimental ML-DSA and SLH-DSA algorithms for issuing PQC certificates.

components.name: Azure Dedicated HSM
components.description: Microsoft Azure Dedicated HSM powered by Thales Luna 7 hardware (FIPS 140-2 L3). Thales Luna firmware 7.9+ adds ML-KEM and ML-DSA support; Azure Dedicated HSM customers can request firmware updates for PQC capabilities. Microsoft Azure Managed HSM (Marvell LiquidSecurity) adding PQC key types per 2029 roadmap.

components.name: InfoSec Global AgileSec
components.description: AgileSec Analytics is a cryptographic discovery and agility platform that identifies quantum-vulnerable cryptography across enterprise systems and orchestrates migration to PQC. FedRAMP Moderate authorized (August 2025). Does not implement PQC algorithms directly — enables organisations to discover, inventory, and migrate their cryptographic assets to NIST-standardised PQC.

components.name: iOS 26 / macOS 16
components.description: System-wide PQC support including PQ3 for iMessage and HPKE with ML-KEM/ML-DSA. APIs for third-party apps via CryptoKit.

components.name: Signal Protocol
components.description: Experimental PQXDH (Post-Quantum Extended Diffie-Hellman) support. Signal's approach to quantum-resistant messaging combining X25519, Kyber, and double-ratchet protocol for forward secrecy.

components.name: OpenPGP.js
components.description: OpenPGP.js PR #2022 ('[v7] PQC: implement ML-KEM-768+X25519 and ML-DSA-65+Ed25519', merged into the v7 branch 2026-07-10) implements draft-ietf-openpgp-pqc: composite ML-KEM-768+X25519 encryption and composite ML-DSA-65+Ed25519 signatures (paired with Ed25519, not ECDSA). Standalone SLH-DSA support is not confirmed in the merged PR. Not yet published to npm as of 2026-08-18 -- available only on the unreleased v7 branch.

components.name: OpenMLS
components.description: OpenMLS PQ branch tracks draft-ietf-mls-pq-ciphersuites-04 (ML-KEM + ML-DSA cipher suites for MLS group messaging).

components.name: mls-rs (AWS)
components.description: mls-rs PQ track: ML-KEM-based cipher suites for MLS, tracking draft-ietf-mls-pq-ciphersuites.

components.name: mlspp
components.description: C++ reference implementation for the MLS protocol. Hybrid post-quantum cipher suites (draft-ietf-mls-pq-ciphersuites) are implemented and merged into the main branch: PR #456 'Add support for hybrid PQ cipher suites' (merged 2025-11-24) and PR #455 'Add support for CFRG Hybrid KEMs' (merged 2025-11-23), built on liboqs with an OpenSSL 1.1 dependency (no PQ support yet on BoringSSL). Pure-PQ (non-hybrid) cipher suites are explicitly not implemented.

components.name: libtpms
components.description: libtpms is a C library providing TPM 2.0 functionality. Tracks TCG TPM 2.0 Library v1.83 (no PQ); v1.85 PQ support in fork branches (incl. pqctoday-tpm).

components.name: swtpm
components.description: swtpm is a libtpms-based software TPM emulator. Tracks libtpms versions; PQ via pqctoday-tpm fork branches.

components.name: pqctoday-tpm
components.description: Fork of swtpm+libtpms adding TCG TPM 2.0 v1.85 RC4 PQ commands (ML-DSA-44/65/87, ML-KEM-512/768/1024, Labeled KEM). Drives the /playground/tpm-playground workshop.

components.name: Eclipse Mosquitto
components.description: Mosquitto 2.x uses OpenSSL for TLS. With OpenSSL 3.5+ and oqs-provider, MQTT TLS connections negotiate X25519MLKEM768 hybrid KEM TLS 1.3 today — no Mosquitto source changes needed. Mosquitto itself has no native PQC code; PQC capability flows from the TLS library. Sandbox test 31 confirms live X25519MLKEM768 MQTT TLS handshakes. Critical for IoT fleet migration: device firmware may need OpenSSL 3.5+ update.

components.name: osslsigncode
components.description: osslsigncode is an open-source Authenticode signing tool for PE/MSI/CAB files using OpenSSL. With OpenSSL 3.6+ linked, ML-DSA-65 signatures can be embedded in PE binaries today via custom OID. Sandbox test 17 demonstrates ML-DSA-65 PE signing and verification. Caveat: Windows Authenticode validation chain does not yet accept ML-DSA OIDs — dual-signing (classical + ML-DSA) is the migration path for cross-platform compatibility. No FIPS validation. Suitable for internal pipeline signing where verifier is under your control.

components.name: OpenBao
components.description: OpenBao is an open-source fork of HashiCorp Vault (donated to LF Edge / OpenBao project, Apache-2.0). It supports PQC TLS for its listener via Go crypto stack (X25519MLKEM768 in Go 1.24+ tls package). The transit secrets engine does NOT yet natively support ML-DSA key generation (unlike Vault Enterprise 1.19+). Migration path: use OpenBao 2.x with Go 1.24+ for PQC transport; pair with oqs-provider for ML-DSA signing via OpenSSL subprocess. Actively tracked in OpenBao GitHub issues. Suitable for OSS-only deployments requiring open-source secrets management.

components.name: wireguard-go
components.description: Userspace WireGuard implementation in Go. Native Noise_IKpsk2 handshake uses Curve25519 (classical). Post-quantum security achieved by injecting an ML-KEM-768-derived shared secret as a 32-byte preshared-key (wg set peer preshared-key), giving Curve25519+ML-KEM hybrid protection against HNDL attacks. Used in pqctoday-sandbox test 29.

components.name: Playwright
components.description: Playwright is a browser automation framework. In the PQC context it validates ML-KEM-768 hybrid TLS connections through real browser engines. Chromium 124+ supports X25519MLKEM768 (kyber hybrid); Firefox has experimental OQS-based PQC TLS. Sandbox scenario 6 navigates Playwright/Chromium to a PQC-TLS nginx server and asserts the negotiated cipher suite includes X25519MLKEM768. Playwright itself has no crypto logic — it exposes the TLS capabilities of the underlying browser engine.

components.name: QKDNetSim
components.description: QKDNetSim is an ns-3 module for simulating quantum key distribution networks. Implements BB84 protocol simulation, QKD link management, key relay across multi-hop networks, and integration with classical cryptographic protocols (IPsec, IKEv2). Enables network engineers to model and evaluate QKD-enhanced security architectures before hardware deployment. Used in sandbox with ns-3 to demonstrate a complete QKD-secured link without physical quantum hardware.

components.name: SeQUeNCe

manufacturer.name: Argonne National Laboratory / University of Chicago

components.description: SeQUeNCe (Simulator of QUantum Network Communication) is a Python-based quantum network simulation framework developed by Argonne National Laboratory and the University of Chicago. Simulates quantum repeaters, entanglement distribution, QKD protocols (BB84, E91), and quantum memory management. Used in sandbox to model quantum internet architecture and key delivery to classical endpoints. Enables researchers to prototype quantum network control planes without physical quantum hardware.

components.name: age (file encryption)
components.description: age v1.3.0 (released Dec 27) adds NATIVE post-quantum recipients based on HPKE with a hybrid ML-KEM-768 KEM (combined with X25519). PQC recipients use the age1pq1... prefix and identities use AGE-SECRET-KEY-PQ-1...; generated via 'age-keygen -pq'. The standalone age-pq/'pq' plugin remains for backward compatibility with pre-1.3 versions. No FIPS 140-3 validation; suitable for secrets-at-rest in cloud-native and GitOps pipelines.

components.name: CBOMkit
components.description: IBM's open-source CBOMkit toolkit generates Cryptography Bills of Materials (CBOM) in CycloneDX 1.6 format. Scans Java and Python source code and Docker images for cryptographic usage, annotating each finding with quantum-vulnerability status aligned to NIST CNSA 2.0. Integrates with OPA for policy enforcement — checking if detected algorithms are quantum-safe. Sandbox scenario cbom-compliance generates a CBOM for a sample application then evaluates it against a no-quantum-vulnerable-crypto Rego policy via OPA, showing real-time compliance violations.

components.name: Open Policy Agent (OPA)
components.description: OPA is a general-purpose policy engine using the Rego policy language for unified authorization across cloud-native stacks. In the PQC migration context, OPA enforces cryptographic policies — blocking Kubernetes deployments that use RSA-2048, flagging TLS configs without ML-KEM, or failing CI pipelines that include quantum-vulnerable algorithms in their CBOM. Sandbox cbom-compliance scenario feeds CBOMkit output to OPA, which evaluates a Rego policy to detect CNSA 2.0 violations and emit structured violation reports. OPA itself has no crypto; it is the policy enforcement layer above crypto discovery tools.

components.name: cdxgen
components.description: cdxgen generates CycloneDX SBOMs and CBOMs across 20+ ecosystems (Go, Python, Java, Rust, Debian/rpm packages, container images). The --include-crypto flag activates cryptographic discovery: it detects algorithm usage in source code and binaries, annotates each component with its cryptographic properties in CycloneDX 1.6 cryptoProperties format, and flags quantum-vulnerable algorithms. Sandbox scenarios use cdxgen to scan the running container filesystem (--type os) to produce a real CBOM covering OpenSSL version, softhsmv3, strongSwan, cosign and all installed tools — which OPA then evaluates against a CNSA 2.0 Rego policy.

components.name: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.2
components.description: RHEL 10.2 GA May 6 2026. Extends RHEL 10.x PQC foundation with additional quantum-resistant features. Ships alongside Red Hat Certificate System 11.0 which integrates NIST-standardized ML-DSA signatures into PKI infrastructure. Defends against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks. Continues unified PQC rollout across Red Hat enterprise Linux portfolio.

components.name: Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform

components.name: Red Hat Certificate System 11.0

Addresses harvest-now-decrypt-later risk for certificate-based authentication and long-lived certificates. Released alongside RHEL 10.2 and 9.8.

components.name: libgcrypt

components.name: libsodium
components.description: Portable fork of NaCl providing modern misuse-resistant primitives. As of 1.0.22 (2026-04-09) it ships post-quantum KEMs: ML-KEM768 (NIST FIPS 203) via crypto_kem_mlkem768_*(), and X-Wing — a hybrid KEM combining ML-KEM768 with X25519 — via crypto_kem_*(), with X-Wing recommended for most applications. SHA-3 (sha3-256/sha3-512) added with one-shot and streaming APIs.

components.name: HPE Aruba ArubaOS-CX

No shipping ArubaOS-CX release announces ML-KEM/ML-DSA data-plane support yet.

ASUS's own ExpertBook Ultra press release (Jan 2026) additionally states BIOS/firmware protection support for ML-KEM (FIPS 203) as part of the ExpertGuardian security architecture: "ExpertBook Ultra strengthens long-term BIOS protection by adding post-quantum cryptography (PQC) into the firmware security layer. With support for NIST-aligned PQC algorithms -- including ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and ML-DSA (FIPS 204) -- it further reinforces the platform chain of trust."

components.name: ASUSTOR Post-Quantum Cryptography Module

components.name: Best PQC MLKEM

components.name: BlackBerry Certicom Security Builder FIPS Module
components.description: The Security Builder FIPS Module implements the NIST PQC standards ML-DSA (FIPS 204), ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205), validated for algorithmic correctness through the NIST ACVP/CAVP program (product 19667), exposed via the Security Builder C/Java cryptographic APIs.

components.name: C-DOT ML-KEM Cryptographic Algorithms

The certificate's approved-algorithms list contains no post-quantum (LMS/HSS or other) algorithms.

components.name: CryptoNext Quantum-Safe Library (C-QSL)

components.name: FortiPQC Software Library

Engineered to meet FIPS 140-3 Level 4, Common Criteria AVA_VAN.5 and SESIP Level 5 certification targets with built-in SCA/FIA protection.

components.name: Futurex GSP4000 Hardware Security Module

components.name: Sansec csmsc1 Cryptographic Module

components.name: Saviynt Cryptographic Module

components.name: Shinewave Post-Quantum Cryptography Module for IoT Gateways

components.name: NESLIB Cryptographic Library (incl. NesLib_PQML)

components.name: STSAFE-V100-TPM
components.description: Common Criteria EAL4+ certified automotive TPM (ANSSI-CC-2024/38) whose firmware images are authenticated using the post-quantum stateful hash-based LMS signature (NIST SP 800-208), allowing future PQC algorithm support via signed field firmware upgrades.

components.name: Synopsys Agile PQC Public Key Accelerator (PKA)

components.name: Tellabs Panorama PON Manager Cryptographic Module
components.description: FIPS 140-3 validated module (CMVP certificate #5130) providing stateful hash-based post-quantum signatures LMS and HSS (per SP 800-208). The module is based on SafeLogic CryptoComply and is integrated into the Panorama PON Manager.

components.name: TQ42 Cryptography
components.description: Implements ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204) and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) across all standardized parameter sets, exposed via the open-source C/C++ library API. All three algorithms are NIST CAVP/ACVP validated (CAVP product #18351).

components.name: Trend Micro Java Crypto Module
components.description: Per the candidate certification data the module supports the stateful hash-based signature schemes LMS and HSS (NIST SP 800-208), validated under FIPS 140-3 (CMVP certificate #5131). These provide quantum-resistant firmware/software signature capability alongside the module's classical algorithms.

components.name: Tutus Farist IEG
components.description: The Farist IEG incorporates FrodoKEM as a quantum-resistant key encapsulation mechanism, as documented in its Common Criteria Security Target. The PQC protection is evaluated and certified under the Swedish (CSEC) Common Criteria scheme.

components.name: Utimaco Quantum Protect (Stateful Hash-Based Signature Module)
components.description: Implements the stateful hash-based signature scheme LMS (NIST SP 800-208), including patented state management for high-availability/backup, exposed through the HSM as part of the Quantum Protect package. LMS is NIST CAVP/ACVP validated (CAVP product #20182).

components.name: WiSECURE CRYSTAL Library (ML-KEM and ML-DSA)
components.description: Implements ML-KEM (FIPS 203; KeyGen and Encap/Decap) and ML-DSA (FIPS 204; KeyGen, SigGen, SigVer), exposed as a software library. Validated via NIST CAVP/ACVP (CAVP product #20095) on the ARM9E operating environment (first validated 2025-08-14).

components.name: wolfCrypt Post Quantum
components.description: Implements ML-KEM (FIPS 203) for key establishment, ML-DSA (FIPS 204) and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) for digital signatures (plus LMS/XMSS verification), exposed through the wolfCrypt library API. The PQC algorithms are NIST CAVP/ACVP validated (CAVP product #21279) and incorporated into wolfCrypt's FIPS 140-3 module.

components.name: pkcs11-provider (pqctoday composite)
components.description: OpenSSL 3.x provider (latchset pkcs11-provider fork + pqctoday-org composite extensions) bridging OpenSSL EVP operations to a PKCS#11 token. In the sandbox it exposes LAMPS draft-19 composite signature OIDs (ML-DSA+Ed25519, ML-DSA+ECDSA) and passes ML-KEM, SLH-DSA and XMSS operations through to the softhsmv3 backend. Built from pqctoday-hsm/src/vendor/pkcs11-provider; drives sandbox scenarios for TLS, VPN, KMS and composite certificates.

components.name: softhsmv3 (pqctoday-hsm fork)
components.description: PQC-enabled fork of SoftHSM2 v2.7.0 (pqctoday-org/pqctoday-hsm), OpenSSL-only EVP backend, PKCS#11 v3.2. Exposes FIPS 203/204/205 mechanisms at vendor codepoints 0x4030+ (0x4032 HSS keygen, 0x4033 SLH-DSA sign/verify, 0x4034 ML-KEM keygen, 0x4035 ML-DSA keygen, 0x4036/0x4037 sign/verify variants). Software token backing softhsmv3 ships at /usr/local/lib/softhsm/libsofthsmv3.so and is the PKCS#11 backend for the sandbox TLS, VPN, KMS, PGP, firmware and TPM scenarios. PyKCS11 0.5.x cannot enumerate the v3.2 mechs; scripts use pkcs11-tool or hard-coded mech IDs.

components.name: composite_mkcert
components.description: In-tree pqctoday C utility (docker/composite_mkcert.c) that generates LAMPS draft-19 composite certificates by calling the pkcs11-provider symbols against softhsmv3. Used in the sandbox hybrid-certificate scenario to mint composite ML-DSA+classical certs. Not an upstream product; lives in the sandbox image build tree.

components.name: opgpkcs11 (openpgp-pkcs11-sequoia bridge)
components.description: openpgp-pkcs11-sequoia bridge (built from pqctoday-hsm/openpgp) that lets Sequoia sq produce OpenPGP v6 signatures backed by ML-DSA keys held in the softhsmv3 PKCS#11 token. Since native ML-DSA in OpenPGP is not yet merged upstream, the PQC keymat is generated externally (PyKCS11 to softhsmv3) and stitched into the OpenPGP v6 envelope by this bridge. Drives the sandbox PGP scenario.

components.name: ssh-audit
components.description: ssh-audit (jtesta) is an SSH server/client configuration auditing tool. It detects and reports post-quantum SSH key-exchange algorithms such as sntrup761x25519-sha512 and mlkem768x25519-sha256 advertised by an endpoint. It is an analysis tool, not a PQC implementation. Used in the sandbox crypto-discovery scenario to confirm PQC SSH kex negotiation.

components.name: pqctoday-kmip
components.description: pqctoday-kmip is pqctoday's own MIT-licensed KMIP 3.0 server, written in Rust and executing crypto on the softhsmrustv3 PKCS#11 v3.2 engine (NOT on ThalesGroup/kmip-go, which an earlier catalog revision recorded in error). It exposes a three-plane architecture: a crypto-agility policy plane, KMIP 3.0 key management, and PKCS#11 crypto execution. Verified by execution on 2026-08-09: ML-DSA-65 Create+Sign and ML-KEM-768 Create+Encapsulate+Decapsulate all succeeded against a live server, with 6 managed objects and an audit trail reporting 37 policy decisions, 78 KMIP operations and 14 PKCS#11 calls. Data-plane TLS is quantum-safe-profiled: TLS 1.3 only with hybrid ML-KEM groups, classical key exchange refused outright.

components.name: age-plugin-pqkem
components.description: age-plugin-pqkem was intended to add a post-quantum (ML-KEM) recipient plugin to the age file-encryption tool for the sandbox SOPS+age scenario. The upstream repository str4d/age-plugin-pqkem returns HTTP 404 (deleted/renamed/private) and the binary is not installed in any sandbox container; the scenario silently falls back to classical age X25519. Tracked here to document the gap. Note: age v1.3.0 now provides native hybrid ML-KEM-768 recipients, superseding the need for this plugin (see the "age (file encryption)" row).

components.name: mtc (Merkle Tree Certificates CLI)
components.description: bwesterb/mtc is a CLI implementing the Merkle Tree Certificates (MTC) CA lifecycle: queue, issue, cert, verify, mirror. The CA signing key is a fixed ML-DSA-87 key. The installed v0.1.2 implements a pre-PLANTS draft revision (api label v04b), differing from draft-ietf-plants-merkle-tree-certs-04. It cannot parse NIST ML-DSA SPKI OIDs, so assertion subject keys fall back to P-256 (disclosed via subject_key_fallback_reason). No TLS stack negotiates MTC in the sandbox; the scenario covers cert management and size only.

components.name: Rosenpass
components.description: Rosenpass is a Rust post-quantum-secure VPN key-exchange daemon. It performs an ML-KEM-based handshake and rotates the WireGuard pre-shared key roughly every 2 minutes, giving WireGuard tunnels post-quantum forward secrecy. In the sandbox it replaces the prior fake-PQC WireGuard script (which used SHA-256 of an ML-KEM public key as the PSK). Architectural note: Rosenpass uses its own internal liboqs PQC backend, NOT the pqctoday-hsm PKCS#11 backend — the only sandbox scenario with this exception, disclosed in the scenario JSON.

components.name: Cryptsoft KMIP & PKCS#11 SDK

First PQC-ready KMIP 3.0 + PKCS#11 v3.2 SDKs (Mar 2025); supports ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204) and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205); completed multi-vendor KMIP PQC interoperability testing. Embedded inside many commercial KMS/HSM products.

components.name: strongSwan (pqctoday-hsm PQC fork)
components.description: strongSwan 6.0.7 patched by pqctoday-hsm (strongswan-pqc.patch, strongswan-pqc-supplement.patch, strongswan-pqc-slhdsa.patch, plus a PKCS#11 plugin patch) to add post-quantum IKEv2 AUTHENTICATION on top of upstream's ML-KEM key exchange. The patches introduce KEY_ML_DSA_44/65/87 and SIGN_ML_DSA_44/65/87 to libstrongswan's key-type and signature-scheme enums, the id-ml-dsa-* OIDs, and proposal keywords (mldsa65 / ike:mldsa65); private keys stay in a softhsmv3 PKCS#11 v3.2 token and are never exported. UPSTREAM strongSwan does NOT ship this -- those enum values do not exist in 6.0.7 and its first-party release notes document ML-KEM key exchange only, with IKEv2 authentication remaining PSK/RSA/ECDSA. See the separate `strongswan` row for the upstream product; this row is the fork.

components.name: softhsmrustv3 (pqctoday Rust PKCS#11 engine)
components.description: Pure-Rust PKCS#11 v3.2 engine, the second crypto backend in pqctoday-hsm alongside the C++ softhsmv3. It is the production backend for the pqctoday-kmip server and the CACP policy engine, and it compiles to wasm32-unknown-emscripten as a staticlib linked into openssl.wasm for the in-browser playground. Carries its own checked-in PKCS#11 v3.2 conformance evidence (rust/RUST_P11_V32_CONFORMANCE_REPORT.md). Since 2026-08-08 it also emits a runtime-gated PKCS#11 operation-evidence log, so a caller can prove which mechanism executed inside the token rather than asserting it.

components.name: bench-harness (pqctoday PKCS#11 benchmark)
components.description: Rust benchmark harness in pqctoday-hsm that drives a PKCS#11 v3.2 engine directly and reports per-mechanism throughput across a 26-algorithm matrix (16 signature, 10 key agreement). It is what the sandbox hsm-perf-bench scenario measures. Published ops/sec figures must come from a run with the engine's operation log DISABLED — at roughly 62,000 signs/sec an enabled log measures the logger rather than the HSM.

components.name: age-plugin-pqctoday
components.description: pqctoday's age recipient plugin implementing the X-Wing hybrid KEM (X25519 + ML-KEM-768) so age — and therefore SOPS — can wrap secrets to a post-quantum recipient. The post-quantum key material is generated in and held by softhsmv3 over PKCS#11 rather than in a file. This is the component that gives the sandbox's SOPS GitOps scenario its PQC; SOPS itself has none (see the getsops-sops row).

components.name: OpenSSL 3.6
components.description: OpenSSL 3.6.x carries ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA natively -- no external provider -- plus the hybrid TLS 1.3 groups (X25519MLKEM768, SecP256r1MLKEM768, SecP384r1MLKEM1024). 3.6 also added LMS signature VERIFICATION support per NIST SP 800-208, present in both the FIPS and default providers (verification only, not key generation or signing). This is the branch the pqctoday sandbox builds every scenario against. IMPORTANT: 3.6 is NOT an LTS branch and reaches end of life on 2026-11-01; the LTS branch is 3.5.x, supported to 2030-04-08, which carries the same PQC algorithm set. Anyone adopting 3.6 for PQC should plan the move to an LTS or later branch before that date.

components.name: Post-quantum cryptography support in TrustCore SDK | DigiCert developer portal
components.description: TrustCore SDK's NanoCrypto module natively implements NIST-standardized PQC algorithms: ML-KEM (FIPS 203, lattice-based KEM, formerly Kyber, parameter sets ML-KEM-512/768/1024), ML-DSA (FIPS 204, lattice-based signatures, formerly Dilithium, parameter sets ML-DSA-44/65/87), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205, stateless hash-based signatures for constrained/embedded devices). Both ML-KEM and ML-DSA expose a QS_* API. NanoSSL adds TLS 1.3 hybrid key-exchange support (X25519MLKEM768, SecP256r1MLKEM768) and pure/composite ML-DSA authentication for server/client certs.

components.name: Cosmos SDK
components.description: Cosmos SDK v0.55.0 (2026-07-27) added ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) as an opt-in validator consensus key type and user account key type: SDK key wrappers, Amino + interface-registry registration, multisig support, mnemonic-based keyring creation/recovery (--algo ml_dsa_65), transaction signing/verification, an ante-handler gas cost, PoA-module support, and genesis import/export for validator key rotation. Existing chains still default to ed25519-only consensus keys in genesis; ML-DSA-65 is available but not yet the production default for any chain the SDK powers.
